sentences.zh: 允禟

translations.literal: Yuntang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuntang.

sentences.zh: 輔國公允䄉履懿親王允祹怡賢親王允祥

translations.literal: Fuguo Gong Yun'e, Prince Luyi Yunyou, Prince Yixian Yinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo Gong Yun'e; Prince Luyi Yunyou; Prince Yixian Yinxiang.

sentences.zh: 恂勤郡王允禵愉恪郡王允潖果毅親王允禮

translations.literal: Prince Xunqin of the Second Rank Yinti, Prince Yukuo of the Second Rank Yunpeng, Prince Guoyi Yunli.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xunqin of the Second Rank Yinti; Prince Yukuo of the Second Rank Yunpeng; Prince Guoyi Yunli.

sentences.zh: 果恭郡王弘適簡靖貝勒允禕慎靖郡王允禧

translations.literal: Prince Guogong of the Second Rank Hongshi, Beile Jianjing Yunyi, Prince Shenjing of the Second Rank Yunxi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guogong of the Second Rank Hongshi; Beile Jianjing Yunyi; Prince Shenjing of the Second Rank Yunxi.

sentences.zh: 質莊親王永瑢恭勤貝勒允祜郡王品級誠貝勒允祁

translations.literal: Prince Zhizhuang Yongrong, Beile Gongqin Yunhu, Beile Cheng of princely rank Yunqi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhizhuang Yongrong; Beile Gongqin Yunhu; Beile Cheng Yunqi, of princely rank.

sentences.zh: 諴恪親王允祕

translations.literal: Prince Xianke Yunbi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xianke Yunbi.

sentences.zh: 端親王弘暉和恭親王弘晝懷親王福惠

translations.literal: Prince Duan Honghui, Prince Hegong Hongzhou, Prince Huai Fuhui.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Duan Honghui; Prince Hegong Hongzhou; Prince Huai Fuhui.

sentences.zh: 聖祖三十五子：孝誠仁皇后生承祜、理密親王允礽，孝恭仁皇后生第六子允祚、世宗、恂勤郡王允禵，敬敏皇貴妃章佳氏生怡賢親王允祥，溫僖貴妃鈕祜祿氏生貝子品級允䄉，順懿密妃王氏生愉恪郡王允潖、莊恪親王允祿、第十八子允祄，純裕勤妃陳氏生果毅親王允禮，惠妃納喇氏生承慶、貝子品級允禔，宜妃郭絡羅氏生恒溫親王允祺、第九子允禟、第十一子允禌，榮妃馬佳氏生承瑞、賽音察渾、長華、長生、誠隱郡王允祉，成妃戴佳氏生淳度，良妃衛氏生第八子允禩，定妃萬琉哈氏生履懿親王允祹，平妃赫舍里氏生允禨，通嬪納喇氏生萬黼、允禶，襄嬪高氏生第十九子允禝、簡靖貝勒允禕，謹嬪色赫圖氏生恭勤貝勒允祜，靜嬪石氏生郡王品級誠貝勒允祁，熙嬪陳氏生慎靖郡王允禧，穆嬪陳氏生諴恪親王允祕，貴人郭絡羅氏生允䄔，貴人陳氏生允禐。

translations.literal: Shengzu had thirty-five sons: Empress Xiaochengren bore Chenghu and Prince Mizhi Yinreng; Empress Xiaogongren bore the sixth son Yunzuo, the Shizong Emperor, and Prince Xunqin Yinti; Imperial Noble Consort Jingmin of the Zhang clan bore Prince Yixian Yinxiang; Consort Wenxi of the Niuhuru clan bore Yun'e of beizi rank; Consort Shunyi of the Wang clan bore Prince Yukuo Yunpeng, Prince Zhuangke Yunlu, and the eighteenth son Yunxu; Consort Chunyu of the Chen clan bore Prince Guoyi Yunli; Consort Hui of the Nara clan bore Chengqing and Yunzhi of beizi rank; Consort Yi of the Guoluoluo clan bore Prince Hengwen Yunqi, the ninth son Yuntang, and the eleventh son Yunxu; Consort Rong of the Ma clan bore Chengrui, Saiyinchahun, Changhua, Changsheng, and Prince Chengyin Yinzhi; Consort Cheng of the Dai clan bore Chundu; Consort Liang of the Wei clan bore the eighth son Yunsi; Consort Ding of the Wanliuha clan bore Prince Luyi Yunyou; Consort Ping of the Hesheri clan bore Yunxi; Lady Tong of the Nara clan bore Wanfu and Yun'e; Lady Xiang of the Gao clan bore the nineteenth son and Beile Jianjing Yunyi; Lady Jin of the Sehetu clan bore Beile Gongqin Yunhu; Lady Jing of the Shi clan bore Beile Cheng Yunqi of princely rank; Lady Xi of the Chen clan bore Prince Shenjing Yunxi; Lady Mu of the Chen clan bore Prince Xianke Yunbi; Lady Guo of the Guoluoluo clan bore Yun'e; Lady Chen bore Yunxu.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi had thirty-five sons. Empress Xiaochengren gave birth to Chenghu and Prince Mizhi Yinreng. Empress Xiaogongren gave birth to the sixth son Yunzuo, the future Yongzheng Emperor, and Prince Xunqin Yinti. Imperial Noble Consort Jingmin, née Zhang, gave birth to Prince Yixian Yinxiang. Consort Wenxi, née Niuhuru, gave birth to Yun'e, who held beizi rank. Consort Shunyi, née Wang, gave birth to Prince Yukuo Yunpeng, Prince Zhuangke Yunlu, and the eighteenth son Yunxu. Consort Chunyu, née Chen, gave birth to Prince Guoyi Yunli. Consort Hui, née Nara, gave birth to Chengqing and Yunzhi, who held beizi rank. Consort Yi, née Guoluoluo, gave birth to Prince Hengwen Yunqi, the ninth son Yuntang, and the eleventh son Yunli. Consort Rong, née Ma, gave birth to Chengrui, Saiyinchahun, Changhua, Changsheng, and Prince Chengyin Yinzhi. Consort Cheng, née Dai, gave birth to Chundu. Consort Liang, née Wei, gave birth to the eighth son Yunsi. Consort Ding, née Wanliuha, gave birth to Prince Luyi Yunyou. Consort Ping, née Hesheri, gave birth to Yunxi. Lady Tong, née Nara, gave birth to Wanfu and Yun'e. Lady Xiang, née Gao, gave birth to the nineteenth son and Beile Jianjing Yunyi. Lady Jin, née Sehetu, gave birth to Beile Gongqin Yunhu. Lady Jing, née Shi, gave birth to Beile Cheng Yunqi, of princely rank. Lady Xi, née Chen, gave birth to Prince Shenjing Yunxi. Lady Mu, née Chen, gave birth to Prince Xianke Yunbi. A lady of the Guo clan gave birth to Yun'e; a lady of the Chen clan gave birth to Yunxu.

sentences.zh: 允祿出為承澤裕親王碩塞後，允祚、允禌、允祄、允禝皆殤，無封。

translations.literal: Yunlu was given out as heir to Prince Chengyu Shuo Sai; Yunzuo, Yunli, Yunxu, and the nineteenth son all died young and received no titles.
translations.idiomatic: Yunlu was adopted as heir to Prince Chengyu Shuo Sai. Yunzuo, Yunli, Yunxu, and the nineteenth son all died in infancy and were never enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 承瑞、承祜、承慶、賽音察渾、長華、長生、萬黼、允禶，允騕、允禨、允禐皆殤，不齒序。

translations.literal: Chengrui, Chenghu, Chengqing, Saiyinchahun, Changhua, Changsheng, Wanfu, Yun'e, Yunjiao, Yunxi, and Yunxu all died young and were not counted in the order of succession.
translations.idiomatic: Chengrui, Chenghu, Chengqing, Saiyinchahun, Changhua, Changsheng, Wanfu, Yun'e, Yunjiao, Yunxi, and Yunxu likewise died young and were not numbered among the sons in the succession.

sentences.zh: 固山貝子品級允禔，聖祖第一子。

translations.literal: Yunzhi of gushan beizi rank was Shengzu's first son.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhi, who held the rank of gushan beizi, was Kangxi's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 上有巡幸，輒從。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went on tour, he always accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor traveled, he went along.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十九年，命副裕親王福全禦噶爾丹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi he was ordered to assist Prince Yu Fucan in resisting Galdan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of the Kangxi reign he was ordered to serve as deputy to Prince Yu Fucan in operations against Galdan.

sentences.zh: 上以允禔聽讒，與福全不協，私自陳奏，慮在軍中僨事，召還京師。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Yunzhi listened to slander, was at odds with Fucan, and made private memorials, feared trouble in the army and recalled him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found that Yunzhi listened to slander, clashed with Fucan, and sent private memorials; fearing discord in the army, he recalled Yunzhi to the capital.

sentences.zh: 未幾，福全師還，命諸王大臣勘鞫。

translations.literal: Before long Fucan's army returned, and the emperor ordered the princes and grand ministers to investigate and try the case.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Fucan's army returned, and the emperor ordered the princes and senior ministers to investigate and adjudicate the matter.

sentences.zh: 福全初欲發允禔在軍中過失，會有嚴旨，戒允禔不得與福全異同，福全乃引罪。

translations.literal: Fucan at first wished to expose Yunzhi's faults in the army, but there came a stern edict warning Yunzhi not to differ from Fucan, and Fucan then took the blame upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fucan had at first intended to expose Yunzhi's misconduct in the field, but a stern edict warned Yunzhi not to oppose Fucan in any way, whereupon Fucan accepted guilt himself.

sentences.zh: 語在福全傳。

translations.literal: The account is in Fucan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: This is recounted in the biography of Fucan.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，從上征噶爾丹，命與內大臣索額圖統先發八旗前鋒、漢軍火器營與四旗察哈爾及綠旗諸軍駐拖陵布喇克待上。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he followed the emperor on the campaign against Galdan and was ordered, together with Inner Minister Songgotu, to command the advance Eight Banner vanguard, the Han Army firearms battalion, four Chahar banners, and the Green Standard forces, encamping at Tuolingbulake to await the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year he accompanied the emperor on the campaign against Galdan and was ordered, with Inner Minister Songgotu, to lead the advance forces—the Eight Banner vanguard, the Han Army firearms battalion, four Chahar banners, and the Green Standard troops—and to encamp at Tuolingbulake until the emperor arrived.

sentences.zh: 西路大將軍費揚古軍後期，下軍中大臣議，亦遣官諮允禔。

translations.literal: The western-route commander-in-chief Fei Yanggu's army was late; the matter was referred to the army's grand ministers for deliberation, and officials were also sent to consult Yunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Commander-in-Chief Fei Yanggu on the western route fell behind schedule, the case was submitted to the army's senior ministers for deliberation, and envoys were also sent to seek Yunzhi's opinion.

sentences.zh: 上遂進軍昭莫多。

translations.literal: The emperor then advanced to Jao Modo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then marched on Jao Modo.

sentences.zh: 既捷，允禔留中拖陵犒軍，尋召還。

translations.literal: After the victory Yunzhi remained at Tuoling to reward the troops and was soon recalled.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory Yunzhi stayed at Tuoling to distribute rewards to the army and was soon recalled.

sentences.zh: 三十七年三月，封直郡王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirty-seventh year he was enfeoffed as Prince Zhi of the Second Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirty-seventh year he was created Prince Zhi of the Second Rank.

sentences.zh: 三十九年四月，上巡視永定河堤，鳩工疏濬，命允禔總之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirty-ninth year the emperor inspected the Yongding River dikes, mobilized labor to dredge them, and ordered Yunzhi to supervise the work.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the thirty-ninth year the emperor inspected the Yongding River dikes, organized labor to dredge them, and put Yunzhi in overall charge.

sentences.zh: 四十七年九月，皇太子允礽既廢，允禔奏曰：「允礽所行卑汙，失人心。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the forty-seventh year, after the crown prince Yinreng had been deposed, Yunzhi memorialized: "Yinreng's conduct is base and filthy and has lost the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the forty-seventh year, after Crown Prince Yinreng had been deposed, Yunzhi memorialized: "Yinreng's conduct is base and shameful and has lost him the people's regard.

sentences.zh: 術士張明德嘗相允禩必大貴。

translations.literal: The diviner Zhang Mingde once read Yunsi's features and said he would surely attain great eminence.
translations.idiomatic: The diviner Zhang Mingde had once read Yunsi's features and declared that he was destined for great eminence.

sentences.zh: 如誅允礽，不必出皇父手。

translations.literal: If Yinreng is to be executed, it need not be by the imperial father's own hand."
translations.idiomatic: If Yinreng is to be put to death, it need not be by the Emperor Father's own hand."

sentences.zh: 」上怒，詔斥允禔凶頑愚昧，並戒諸皇子勿縱屬下人生事。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and issued an edict denouncing Yunzhi as vicious, obstinate, and stupid, and also warned all the princes not to let their subordinates stir up trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. An edict denounced Yunzhi as vicious, stubborn, and foolish, and warned all the princes not to let their followers make trouble.

sentences.zh: 允禔用喇嘛巴漢格隆魘術魘廢太子，事發，上命監守。

translations.literal: Yunzhi had employed the Lama Bahangelong's sorcery to bewitch and bring down the crown prince; when the affair came to light the emperor ordered him placed under guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhi had used the Lama Bahangelong's sorcery to curse the crown prince; when the plot was exposed the emperor ordered him placed under guard.

sentences.zh: 尋奪爵，幽於第。

translations.literal: Soon his title was stripped and he was confined in his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his title was revoked and he was confined to his mansion.

sentences.zh: 四月，上將巡塞外，諭：「允禔鎮魘皇太子及諸皇子，不念父母兄弟，事無顧忌。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, as the emperor was about to tour beyond the passes, he instructed: "Yunzhi has used sorcery against the crown prince and the other princes, heedless of parents and brothers and without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, as the emperor was about to tour the frontier, he said: "Yunzhi has used sorcery against the crown prince and the other princes. He gives no thought to parents or brothers and acts without restraint.

sentences.zh: 萬一禍發，朕在塞外，三日後始聞，何由制止？

translations.literal: If disaster should break out, I shall be beyond the passes and would not hear of it until three days later—how could it be stopped?"
translations.idiomatic: If trouble should break out while I am beyond the passes, I would not hear of it for three days—how could it be stopped?"

sentences.zh: 」下諸王大臣議，於八旗遣護軍參領八、護軍校八、護軍八十，仍於允禔府中監守。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the princes and grand ministers for deliberation; from the Eight Banners eight guard company commanders, eight guard lieutenants, and eighty guards were dispatched to continue guarding Yunzhi in his mansion.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the princes and senior ministers. From the Eight Banners eight guard company commanders, eight guard lieutenants, and eighty guards were sent to keep watch in Yunzhi's mansion.

sentences.zh: 上復遣貝勒延壽，貝子蘇努，公鄂飛，都統辛泰，護軍統領圖爾海、陳泰，並八旗章京十七人，更番監守，仍嚴諭疏忽當族誅。

translations.literal: The emperor further sent Beile Yanshou, Beizi Sunu, Duke Efei, Banner General Xintai, Guard Commanders Tu'erhai and Chentai, and seventeen clerks of the Eight Banners to take turns guarding him, sternly warning that negligence would bring extinction of the clan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent Beile Yanshou, Beizi Sunu, Duke Efei, Banner General Xintai, Guard Commanders Tu'erhai and Chentai, and seventeen clerks from the Eight Banners to relieve one another in guarding him, with a stern warning that anyone negligent would bring extinction upon his clan.

sentences.zh: 雍正十二年，卒，世宗命以固山貝子禮殯葬。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yongzheng he died; the Shizong Emperor ordered him buried with the rites of a gushan beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of the Yongzheng reign he died, and the Yongzheng Emperor ordered him buried with the rites due a gushan beizi.

sentences.zh: 子弘昉，襲鎮國公。

translations.literal: His son Hongfang inherited as Duke of the State Supporting the Nation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongfang inherited the title of Duke of the State Supporting the Nation.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子永揚，襲輔國公。

translations.literal: His son Yongyang inherited as Duke of the State Assisting the Nation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongyang inherited the title of Duke of the State Assisting the Nation.

sentences.zh: 坐事，奪爵。

translations.literal: He was implicated in a case and his title was taken away.
translations.idiomatic: He was convicted in a case and stripped of his title.

sentences.zh: 高宗以允禔第十三子弘晌封奉恩將軍，世襲。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor enfeoffed Yunzhi's thirteenth son Hongshang as General by Grace, with hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor enfeoffed Yunzhi's thirteenth son Hongshang as General by Grace, with the title to pass in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 理密親王允礽，聖祖第二子。

translations.literal: Prince Mizhi Yinreng was Shengzu's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mizhi Yinreng was Kangxi's second son.

sentences.zh: 康熙十四年十二月乙丑，聖祖以太皇太后、皇太后命立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, day yichou, of the fourteenth year of Kangxi, Shengzu, by order of the Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress Dowager, established him as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou in the twelfth month of the fourteenth year of the Kangxi reign, Kangxi, acting on the command of the Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress Dowager, installed him as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子方幼，上親教之讀書。

translations.literal: The crown prince was still young, and the emperor personally taught him to read.
translations.idiomatic: While the crown prince was still young, the emperor personally taught him to read.

sentences.zh: 六歲就傅，令大學士張英、李光地為之師，又命大學士熊賜履授以性理諸書。

translations.literal: At six he received a tutor; the emperor made Grand Secretaries Zhang Ying and Li Guangdi his teachers and also ordered Grand Secretary Xiong Cilu to instruct him in the books of Neo-Confucian principle.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of six he was given tutors. The emperor appointed Grand Secretaries Zhang Ying and Li Guangdi as his teachers and ordered Grand Secretary Xiong Cilu to instruct him in Neo-Confucian texts.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，上召江寧巡撫湯斌，以禮部尚書領詹事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the emperor summoned Jiangning Governor Tang Bin and made him Minister of Rites with concurrent appointment as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year the emperor summoned Jiangning Governor Tang Bin and appointed him Minister of Rites while also making him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 斌薦起原任直隸大名道耿介為少詹事，輔導太子。

translations.literal: Bin recommended and recalled the former Zhili Daming Circuit Intendant Geng Jie as Junior Tutor to assist in guiding the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin recommended the former Zhili Daming Circuit Intendant Geng Jie for recall and appointed him Junior Tutor to assist in guiding the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 介旋以疾辭。

translations.literal: Jie soon resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jie soon resigned, citing illness.

sentences.zh: 逾年，斌亦卒。

translations.literal: The following year Bin also died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Tang Bin also died.

sentences.zh: 太子通滿、漢文字，嫻騎射，從上行幸，賡詠斐然。

translations.literal: The crown prince mastered Manchu and Chinese script, was skilled in riding and archery, accompanied the emperor on tours, and composed verse with notable elegance.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince mastered Manchu and Chinese writing, was skilled in riding and archery, accompanied the emperor on his travels, and composed verse of notable elegance.

sentences.zh: 二十九年七月，上親征噶爾丹，駐蹕古魯富爾堅嘉渾噶山，遘疾，召太子及皇三子允祉至行宮。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-ninth year the emperor personally campaigned against Galdan and halted at Gurufurjianggahunga Mountain, where he fell ill and summoned the crown prince and the third prince Yinzhi to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-ninth year the emperor led a campaign against Galdan and halted at Gurufurjianggahunga Mountain, where he fell ill and summoned the crown prince and the third prince Yinzhi to his traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 太子侍疾無憂色，上不懌，遣太子先還。

translations.literal: The crown prince attended him in illness without a look of concern; the emperor was displeased and sent the crown prince back first.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince attended him without showing concern, which displeased the emperor, and he sent the crown prince back ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，禮部奏祭奉先殿儀注，太子拜褥置檻內，上諭尚書沙穆哈移設檻外，沙穆哈請旨記檔，上命奪沙穆哈官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year the Ministry of Rites reported the ritual for sacrifice at the Hall of Imperial Ancestors, placing the crown prince's kneeling mat inside the railing; the emperor instructed Minister Shamoha to move it outside the railing; Shamoha asked that the order be recorded in the archives, and the emperor ordered Shamoha's office taken away.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year the Ministry of Rites submitted the ritual for sacrifice at the Hall of Imperial Ancestors with the crown prince's kneeling mat placed inside the railing. The emperor instructed Minister Shamoha to move it outside. Shamoha asked that the order be entered in the record, and the emperor stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，冊石氏為太子妃。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year Lady Shi was invested as crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year Lady Shi was invested as the crown princess.

sentences.zh: 三十五年二月，上再親征噶爾丹，命太子代行郊祀禮；

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirty-fifth year the emperor again personally campaigned against Galdan and ordered the crown prince to perform the suburban sacrifices in his stead;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the thirty-fifth year the emperor again led a campaign against Galdan and ordered the crown prince to perform the suburban sacrifices on his behalf;

sentences.zh: 各部院奏章，聽太子處理；

translations.literal: memorials from all boards and courts were to be handled by the crown prince;
translations.idiomatic: memorials from all boards and courts were to be handled by the crown prince;

sentences.zh: 事重要，諸大臣議定，啟太子。

translations.literal: important matters were to be deliberated by the grand ministers and then reported to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: on important matters the senior ministers were to deliberate first and then report to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 六月，上破噶爾丹，還，太子迎於諾海河朔，命太子先還。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the emperor defeated Galdan and returned; the crown prince met him north of the Nuo River, and the emperor ordered the crown prince to return first.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the emperor defeated Galdan and returned. The crown prince met him north of the Nuo River, but the emperor ordered him to go back first.

sentences.zh: 上至京師，太子率群臣郊迎。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached the capital the crown prince led the officials in suburban welcome.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached the capital, the crown prince led the officials in a suburban welcome.

sentences.zh: 明年，上行兵寧夏，仍命太子居守。

translations.literal: The next year, when the emperor marched on Ningxia, he again ordered the crown prince to remain and guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the emperor marched on Ningxia, he again left the crown prince in charge at the capital.

sentences.zh: 有為蜚語聞上者，謂太子暱比匪人，素行遂變。

translations.literal: Slander reached the emperor saying the crown prince kept company with worthless men and his former conduct had changed.
translations.idiomatic: Slander reached the emperor claiming that the crown prince kept company with worthless men and that his conduct had changed.

sentences.zh: 上還京師，錄太子左右用事者置於法。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital he arrested the crown prince's close associates who wielded power and punished them by law.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital he arrested the crown prince's powerful associates and punished them according to law.

sentences.zh: 自此眷愛漸替。

translations.literal: From this time his favor gradually waned.
translations.idiomatic: From this point the emperor's affection for him gradually cooled.

sentences.zh: 四十七年八月，上行圍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the forty-seventh year the emperor went on the autumn hunt.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the forty-seventh year the emperor went on the autumn hunt.

sentences.zh: 皇十八子允祄疾作，留永安拜昂阿。

translations.literal: The eighteenth prince Yunxu fell ill and was left at Yong'an Bayang'a.
translations.idiomatic: The eighteenth prince Yunxu fell ill and was left behind at Yong'an Bayang'a.

sentences.zh: 上回鑾臨視，允祄病篤。

translations.literal: The emperor turned back his carriage to visit him; Yunxu's illness was grave.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned back to visit him, but Yunxu's illness was already grave.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「允祄病無濟，區區稚子，有何關係？

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "Yunxu's illness cannot be cured; he is but a small child—what does it matter?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Yunxu's illness cannot be cured. He is only a small child—what does it matter?

sentences.zh: 至於朕躬，上恐貽高年皇太后之憂，下則係天下臣民之望，宜割愛就道。

translations.literal: As for my own person, above I fear causing grief to the aged Grand Empress Dowager, below I am bound to the hopes of all the officials and people under Heaven—I should set aside affection and resume the journey."
translations.idiomatic: As for myself, above I would grieve the aged Grand Empress Dowager, and below the officials and people of the realm depend on me. I must set aside personal sorrow and continue on my way."

sentences.zh: 」因啟蹕。

translations.literal: He then resumed the imperial progress.
translations.idiomatic: He then resumed the imperial progress.

sentences.zh: 九月乙亥，次佈爾哈蘇台，召太子，集諸王大臣諭曰：「允礽不法祖德，不遵朕訓，暴戾淫亂，朕包容二十年矣。

translations.literal: On day yihai in the ninth month, halting at Bu'erhasutai, he summoned the crown prince, assembled the princes and grand ministers, and instructed: "Yinreng does not follow the virtue of the ancestors or obey my teachings; he is violent, cruel, and dissolute. I have borne with him for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai in the ninth month, while halted at Bu'erhasutai, he summoned the crown prince, assembled the princes and senior ministers, and declared: "Yinreng does not honor the virtue of our ancestors or heed my instruction. He is violent, cruel, and dissolute. I have borne with him for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 乃其惡愈張，僇辱廷臣，專擅威權，鳩聚黨與，窺伺朕躬起居動作。

translations.literal: Yet his wickedness has grown ever more rampant: he insults and humiliates court ministers, monopolizes authority, gathers factions, and spies on my comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his wickedness has only grown. He insults court ministers, monopolizes power, gathers factions, and spies on my every movement.

sentences.zh: 平郡王訥爾素、貝勒海善、公普奇遭其毆撻，大臣官員亦罹其毒。

translations.literal: Prince Ping of the Second Rank Ne'ersu, Beile Haishan, and Duke Puqi have suffered his beatings, and grand ministers and officials have also fallen victim to his malice.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ping of the Second Rank Ne'ersu, Beile Haishan, and Duke Puqi have been beaten by him, and senior ministers and officials have likewise suffered at his hands.

sentences.zh: 朕巡幸陝西、江南、浙江，未嘗一事擾民。

translations.literal: On my tours to Shaanxi, Jiangnan, and Zhejiang I never once disturbed the people.
translations.idiomatic: On my tours to Shaanxi, Jiangnan, and Zhejiang I never once troubled the people.

sentences.zh: 允礽與所屬恣行乖戾，無所不至，遣使邀截蒙古貢使，攘進御之馬，致蒙古俱不心服。

translations.literal: Yinreng and his followers wantonly acted perversely in every way, sent agents to intercept Mongol tribute envoys, seized horses presented to the throne, and caused the Mongols to lose heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yinreng and his followers acted with unrestrained perversity in every regard. They sent agents to intercept Mongol tribute envoys, seized horses presented to the throne, and caused the Mongols to lose all respect.

sentences.zh: 朕以其賦性奢侈，用凌普為內務府總管，以為允礽乳母之夫，便其徵索。

translations.literal: Because he was by nature extravagant, I appointed Ling Pu superintendent of the Imperial Household Department, as husband to Yinreng's wet nurse, to facilitate his exactions.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing his extravagant nature, I appointed Ling Pu superintendent of the Imperial Household Department—he was the husband of Yinreng's wet nurse—so that Yinreng could more easily extort what he wanted.

sentences.zh: 凌普更為貪婪，包衣下人無不怨憾。

translations.literal: Ling Pu became even more greedy, and none of the bondservants under him were without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Pu became even greedier, and every bondservant under him seethed with resentment.

sentences.zh: 皇十八子抱病，諸臣以朕年高，無不為朕憂，允礽乃親兄，絕無友愛之意。

translations.literal: The eighteenth prince lay ill; all the ministers, considering my advanced age, were anxious on my account, yet Yinreng, his own elder brother, showed not the slightest brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: When the eighteenth prince fell ill, every minister, mindful of my advanced age, was anxious on my behalf, yet Yinreng, his own elder brother, showed not the slightest brotherly concern.

sentences.zh: 朕加以責讓，忿然發怒，每夜偪近布城，裂縫竊視。

translations.literal: When I reproached him he flared up in anger; every night he pressed close to the cloth wall of my quarters and peered through the cracks.
translations.idiomatic: When I reproached him he flew into a rage. Every night he crept close to the cloth partition around my quarters and peered through the cracks.

sentences.zh: 從前索額圖欲謀大事，朕知而誅之，今允礽欲為復仇。

translations.literal: Formerly Songgotu plotted a great affair; I discovered it and executed him. Now Yinreng seeks revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Songgotu plotted treason; I discovered it and put him to death. Now Yinreng seeks revenge.

sentences.zh: 朕不卜今日被鴆、明日遇害，晝夜戒慎不寧。

translations.literal: I cannot tell whether today I shall be poisoned or tomorrow murdered; day and night I am on guard and cannot rest.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot know whether I shall be poisoned today or murdered tomorrow. Day and night I live in dread and cannot rest.

sentences.zh: 似此不孝不仁，太祖、太宗、世祖所締造，朕所治平之天下，斷不可付此人！

translations.literal: One so unfilial and inhumane—the realm forged by Taizu, Taizong, and Shizu and brought to peace by me—must on no account be entrusted to such a man!"
translations.idiomatic: A man so unfilial and cruel—the realm forged by Taizu, Taizong, and Shizu and brought to peace under my rule—must never be entrusted to such a person!"

sentences.zh: 」上且諭且泣，至於僕地，即日執允礽，命直郡王允禔監之，誅索額圖二子格爾芬、阿爾吉善，及允礽左右二格、蘇爾特、哈什太、薩爾邦阿；

translations.literal: As the emperor spoke and wept he fell prostrate; that same day Yinreng was seized and Prince Zhi Yunzhi was ordered to guard him; Songgotu's two sons Ge'erfen and A'erjishan were executed, together with Yinreng's close attendants Erge, Su'erte, Hashitai, and Sa'erbang'a;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spoke through his tears until he collapsed prostrate. That same day Yinreng was seized and Prince Zhi Yunzhi was ordered to guard him. Songgotu's sons Ge'erfen and A'erjishan were executed, along with Yinreng's close attendants Erge, Su'erte, Hashitai, and Sa'erbang'a;

sentences.zh: 其罪稍減者，遣戍盛京。

translations.literal: those whose crimes were somewhat lighter were banished to garrison duty at Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: those whose crimes were somewhat lighter were banished to garrison duty at Mukden.

sentences.zh: 次日，上命宣諭諸臣及侍衛官兵，略謂：「允礽為太子，有所使令，眾敢不從，即其中豈無奔走逢迎之人？

translations.literal: The next day the emperor ordered an announcement to the ministers and guard officers and troops, saying in substance: "As crown prince Yinreng gave orders—who would have dared disobey? Among them were there not those who rushed to flatter him?
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor ordered an announcement to the ministers and guard officers and troops, saying in substance: "As crown prince, Yinreng gave orders—who would have dared refuse? Surely some among you rushed to flatter him.

sentences.zh: 今事內干連應誅者已誅，應遣者已遣，餘不更推求，毋危懼。

translations.literal: Now among those implicated who deserved execution have been executed and those who deserved banishment have been banished; the rest will not be pursued further—do not be afraid."
translations.idiomatic: Those implicated who deserved death have been put to death, and those who deserved banishment have been banished. The rest will not be pursued further. Do not be afraid."

sentences.zh: 上既廢太子，憤懣不已，六夕不安寢，召扈從諸臣涕泣言之，諸臣皆嗚咽。

translations.literal: After deposing the crown prince the emperor's anger and grief would not cease; for six nights he could not sleep peacefully and summoned the ministers accompanying him, speaking through tears; all the ministers sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: After deposing the crown prince the emperor could not shake his anger and grief. For six nights he slept fitfully and summoned the ministers in his retinue, speaking through his tears; all of them sobbed.

sentences.zh: 既又諭諸臣，謂：「觀允礽行事，與人大不同，類狂易之疾，似有鬼物憑之者。

translations.literal: He then again instructed the ministers, saying: "Observing Yinreng's conduct, it is utterly unlike other men's, resembling the illness of mania; it seems as though some demon possessed him."
translations.idiomatic: He then told the ministers again: "Judging from Yinreng's conduct, it is utterly unlike that of other men. It resembles mania, as though some evil spirit possessed him."

sentences.zh: 」及還京，設氈帷上駟院側，令允礽居焉，更命皇四子與允禔同守之。

translations.literal: When he returned to the capital he set up a felt tent beside the Upper Stud Farm and had Yinreng dwell there, further ordering the fourth prince and Yunzhi jointly to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to the capital he pitched a felt tent beside the Upper Stud Farm and had Yinreng live there, further ordering the fourth prince and Yunzhi to guard him jointly.

sentences.zh: 尋以廢太子詔宣示天下，上並親撰文告天​​地、太廟、社稷曰：「臣祗承丕緒，四十七年餘矣，於國計民生，夙夜兢業，無事不可質諸天地。

translations.literal: Soon the edict deposing the crown prince was proclaimed throughout the realm, and the emperor also personally composed a text reporting to Heaven and Earth, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the Altar of Land and Grain: "Your subject reverently received the great succession more than forty-seven years ago; in state affairs and the people's livelihood I have labored day and night, and in nothing have I failed to answer before Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the edict deposing the crown prince was proclaimed throughout the realm. The emperor also personally composed a memorial reporting to Heaven and Earth, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the Altar of Land and Grain: "Your subject reverently received the great succession more than forty-seven years ago. In state affairs and the people's livelihood I have labored day and night, and in nothing have I failed to answer before Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 稽古史冊，興亡雖非一轍，而得深懼祖宗垂貽之大業自臣而隳，故身雖不德，而親握朝綱，一切政務，不徇偏私，不謀群小，事無久稽，悉由獨斷，亦惟鞠躬盡瘁，死而後已，在位一日，勤求治理，斷不敢少懈。

translations.literal: Examining the ancient histories, rise and fall have not followed a single path, yet I have deeply feared that the great enterprise bequeathed by the ancestors might perish through me; therefore, though lacking in virtue myself, I have personally held the reins of government. In all affairs of state I have not indulged partiality, not plotted with petty men, allowed nothing to linger long, and decided everything by my own judgment, striving only to exhaust myself in service until death, and while in office for a single day diligently seeking good governance—I have never dared slacken in the least.
translations.idiomatic: The histories show that rise and fall follow many paths, yet I have deeply feared that the great enterprise bequeathed by the ancestors might perish through me. Though lacking in personal virtue, I have held the reins of government myself. In all affairs of state I have refused partiality, refused to plot with petty men, allowed nothing to linger, and decided everything on my own. I have striven to exhaust myself in service until death, and for every day in office I have sought good governance without daring the slightest slackening.

sentences.zh: 不知臣有何辜，生子如允礽者，不孝不義，暴虐慆淫，若非鬼物憑附，狂易成疾，有血氣者豈忍為之？

translations.literal: I know not what guilt your subject has committed to bear a son like Yinreng—unfilial and unjust, violent and dissolute. Unless some demon possessed him and mania took hold, could any man of flesh and blood bear to act thus?
translations.idiomatic: I know not what guilt your subject has committed to bear a son like Yinreng—unfilial, unjust, violent, and dissolute. Unless some evil spirit possessed him and mania took hold, what man of flesh and blood could bear to act thus?

sentences.zh: 允礽口不道忠信之言，身不履德義之行，咎戾多端，難以承祀，用是昭告昊天上帝，特行廢斥，勿致貽憂邦國，痛毒蒼生。

translations.literal: Yinreng's mouth speaks no words of loyalty and faith, his person follows no conduct of virtue and righteousness; his crimes are many and he cannot inherit the sacrifices. Therefore I proclaim to the Supreme Lord of Vast Heaven and specially carry out his deposition, lest he bring grief to the state and pain to the black-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: Yinreng's mouth speaks no word of loyalty or faith, and his person follows no path of virtue or righteousness. His crimes are many and he cannot inherit the sacrifices. Therefore I proclaim to the Supreme Lord of Vast Heaven and hereby depose him, lest he bring grief to the state and suffering to the people.

sentences.zh: 抑臣更有哀籥者，臣自幼而孤，未得親承父母之訓子，遠不及臣，如大清歷數綿長，延臣壽命，臣當益加勤勉，謹保終始；

translations.literal: Moreover your subject has a further sorrow: from childhood I was orphaned and did not personally receive my parents' instruction in raising a son—far inferior to me. If the Qing dynasty's mandate is long and my life is prolonged, your subject should redouble diligence and guard the beginning and end;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has yet another sorrow. From childhood I was orphaned and never received my parents' instruction in raising a son—how far my son falls short of me. If the Qing dynasty's mandate is long and my life is prolonged, I shall redouble my diligence and guard my course to the end;

sentences.zh: 如我國家無福，即殃及臣躬，以全臣令名。

translations.literal: if our state lacks fortune, let the calamity fall on my person alone to preserve my good name.
translations.idiomatic: but if our state lacks fortune, let the calamity fall on me alone, so that my good name may be preserved.

sentences.zh: 臣不勝痛切，謹告。

translations.literal: Your subject cannot bear the anguish and respectfully reports.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject is overcome with anguish and respectfully reports.

sentences.zh: 太子既廢，上諭：「諸皇子中如有謀為皇太子者，即國之賊，法所不宥。

translations.literal: After the crown prince was deposed the emperor instructed: "Among the princes, whoever plots to become crown prince is a traitor to the state and will not be spared by law.
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince was deposed the emperor declared: "Among the princes, whoever plots to become crown prince is a traitor to the state and will not be spared by law.

sentences.zh: 」諸皇子中皇八子允禩謀最力，上知之，命執付議政大臣議罪，削貝勒。

translations.literal: Among the princes the eighth prince Yunsi plotted most vigorously; the emperor knew it and ordered him seized and handed to the Deliberative Princes and Ministers for judgment on his crime; his beile title was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Among the princes the eighth prince Yunsi plotted most vigorously. The emperor learned of it, ordered him seized and handed to the Deliberative Princes and Ministers for judgment, and stripped him of his beile title.

sentences.zh: 十月，皇三子允祉發喇嘛巴漢格隆，為皇長子允禔厭允礽事。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the third prince Yinzhi exposed the Lama Bahangelong in the affair by which the eldest prince Yunzhi used sorcery against Yinreng.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the third prince Yinzhi exposed the Lama Bahangelong in the affair by which the eldest prince Yunzhi had used sorcery against Yinreng.

sentences.zh: 上令侍衛發允礽所居，得厭勝物十餘事。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered guards to search Yinreng's residence and more than ten sorcery objects were found.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered guards to search Yinreng's residence and found more than ten objects used for sorcery.

sentences.zh: 上幸南苑行圍，遘疾，還宮，召允礽入見，使居咸安宮。

translations.literal: The emperor went to the Southern Park for the hunt, fell ill, returned to the palace, summoned Yinreng for an audience, and had him dwell in the Xian'an Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to the Southern Park for the hunt, fell ill, and returned to the palace. He summoned Yinreng for an audience and had him live in the Xian'an Palace.

sentences.zh: 上逾諸近臣曰：「朕召見允礽，詢問前事，竟有全不知者，是其諸惡皆被魘魅而然。

translations.literal: The emperor told his close ministers: "When I summoned Yinreng and questioned him about past affairs, he knew nothing at all—his every wicked act was due to sorcery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his close ministers: "When I summoned Yinreng and questioned him about past affairs, he knew nothing at all. His every wicked act, it seems, was the work of sorcery.

sentences.zh: 果蒙天佑，狂疾頓除，改而為善，朕自有裁奪。

translations.literal: If truly blessed by Heaven his madness is suddenly removed and he turns to goodness, I shall judge for myself."
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven truly blesses him and his madness is lifted so that he turns to goodness, I shall judge for myself."

sentences.zh: 」廷臣希旨有請復立允礽為太子者，上不許。

translations.literal: Court ministers, reading the emperor's intent, petitioned to restore Yinreng as crown prince; the emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the emperor's intent, some court ministers petitioned to restore Yinreng as crown prince, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 左副都御史勞之辨奏上，上斥其奸詭，奪官，予杖。

translations.literal: Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Lao Zhibian memorialized; the emperor denounced him as treacherous and cunning, stripped his office, and had him beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Lao Zhibian submitted a memorial; the emperor denounced him as treacherous and deceitful, stripped him of office, and had him beaten with the rod.

sentences.zh: 既，上召諸大臣，命於諸皇子中舉孰可繼立為太子者，諸大臣舉允禩。

translations.literal: Thereafter the emperor summoned the grand ministers and ordered them to name among the princes who could succeed as crown prince; the ministers named Yunsi.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the emperor summoned the senior ministers and ordered them to name which prince could succeed as crown prince. The ministers named Yunsi.

sentences.zh: 明日，上召諸大臣入見，諭以太子因魘魅失本性狀。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor summoned the ministers for an audience and instructed them on how the crown prince had lost his true nature through sorcery.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor summoned the ministers and explained how the crown prince had lost his true nature through sorcery.

sentences.zh: 諸大臣奏：「上既灼知太子病源，治療就痊，請上頒旨宣示。

translations.literal: The ministers memorialized: "Your Majesty has clearly known the source of the crown prince's illness; treatment has brought recovery. We beg Your Majesty to issue an edict proclaiming this."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers memorialized: "Your Majesty has clearly identified the source of the crown prince's illness, and treatment has brought recovery. We beg Your Majesty to issue an edict proclaiming this."

sentences.zh: 」又明日，召允礽及諸大臣同入見，命釋之，且曰：「覽古史冊，太子既廢，常不得其死，人君靡不悔者。

translations.literal: The next day again he summoned Yinreng and the ministers together for an audience, ordered his release, and said: "Reading the ancient histories, once a crown prince is deposed he often does not die a natural death, and no ruler fails to regret it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he summoned Yinreng and the ministers together, ordered his release, and said: "Reading the histories, once a crown prince is deposed he seldom dies a natural death, and no ruler fails to regret it.

sentences.zh: 前執允礽，朕日日不釋於懷。

translations.literal: When I earlier seized Yinreng, day after day I could not put it from my mind.
translations.idiomatic: When I earlier seized Yinreng, day after day I could not put it from my mind.

sentences.zh: 自頃召見一次，胸中乃疏快一次。

translations.literal: Since summoning him each time, my breast has grown lighter once more.
translations.idiomatic: Each time I have summoned him since, my heart has grown lighter.

sentences.zh: 今事已明白，明日為始，朕當霍然矣。

translations.literal: Now the matter is clear; from tomorrow onward I shall be entirely relieved."
translations.idiomatic: Now the matter is clear. From tomorrow onward I shall be entirely at ease."

sentences.zh: 」又明日，諸大臣奏請復立允礽為太子，疏留中未下。

translations.literal: The next day again the ministers memorialized to restore Yinreng as crown prince; the memorial was retained at court and not promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the ministers again memorialized to restore Yinreng as crown prince. The memorial was retained at court and not promulgated.

sentences.zh: 上疾漸愈，四十八年正月，諸大臣复疏請，上許之。

translations.literal: As the emperor's illness gradually improved, in the first month of the forty-eighth year the ministers again memorialized, and the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor gradually recovered, in the first month of the forty-eighth year the ministers memorialized again, and the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 三月辛巳，復立允礽為皇太子，妃復為皇太子妃。

translations.literal: On day xinsi in the third month Yinreng was again established as crown prince, and his consort again as crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi in the third month Yinreng was again installed as crown prince, and his consort again as crown princess.

sentences.zh: 五十年十月，上察諸大臣為太子結黨會飲，譴責步軍統領託合齊，尚書耿額、齊世武，都統鄂繕、迓圖。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fiftieth year the emperor discovered that grand ministers had formed factions for the crown prince and held drinking gatherings, and rebuked Infantry Commander Tuoheqi, Ministers Geng'e and Qishiwu, and Banner Generals Echan and Yatu.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fiftieth year the emperor discovered that senior ministers had formed factions around the crown prince and held drinking gatherings. He rebuked Infantry Commander Tuoheqi, Ministers Geng'e and Qishiwu, and Banner Generals Echan and Yatu.

sentences.zh: 託合齊兼坐受戶部缺主沈天生賄罪，絞；

translations.literal: Tuoheqi was also convicted of accepting bribes from Shen Tiansheng, chief clerk of a vacancy in the Ministry of Revenue, and was strangled;
translations.idiomatic: Tuoheqi was also convicted of accepting bribes from Shen Tiansheng, chief clerk of a vacancy in the Ministry of Revenue, and was strangled;

sentences.zh: 又以鎮國公景熙首告貪婪不法諸事，未決，死於獄，命剉屍焚之。

translations.literal: Duke of the State Supporting the Nation Jingxi had been the first to report his greed and unlawful acts; before the case was decided he died in prison, and the emperor ordered his corpse dismembered and burned.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of the State Supporting the Nation Jingxi had been the first to report his greed and unlawful conduct. Before the case was decided he died in prison, and the emperor ordered his corpse dismembered and burned.

sentences.zh: 齊世武、耿額亦以得沈天生賄，絞死。

translations.literal: Qishiwu and Geng'e were also strangled for receiving bribes from Shen Tiansheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qishiwu and Geng'e were likewise strangled for receiving bribes from Shen Tiansheng.

sentences.zh: 鄂繕奪官，幽禁。

translations.literal: Echan was stripped of office and placed in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: Echan was stripped of office and confined.

sentences.zh: 迓圖入辛者庫，守安親王墓。

translations.literal: Yatu was sent to the Sinners' Department to guard Prince An's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Yatu was sent to the Sinners' Department to guard the tomb of Prince An.

sentences.zh: 上諭謂：「諸事皆因允礽。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "All these affairs stem from Yinreng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "All these affairs stem from Yinreng.

sentences.zh: 允礽不仁不孝，徒以言語貨財囑此輩貪得諂媚之人，潛通消息，尤無恥之甚。

translations.literal: Yinreng is unkind and unfilial, merely using words and goods to commission these greedy, fawning men to pass secret messages—utterly shameless in the extreme."
translations.idiomatic: Yinreng is cruel and unfilial. He merely uses words and money to set these greedy flatterers to pass secret messages—the height of shamelessness."

sentences.zh: 五十一年十月，复廢太子，禁錮咸安宮。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifty-first year the crown prince was again deposed and confined in the Xian'an Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fifty-first year the crown prince was again deposed and confined in the Xian'an Palace.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，趙申喬疏請立太子，上諭曰：「建儲大事，未可輕言。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year Zhao Shenqiao memorialized requesting the establishment of a crown prince; the emperor instructed: "The great matter of establishing an heir must not be spoken of lightly.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year Zhao Shenqiao memorialized requesting the establishment of a crown prince. The emperor said: "The great matter of establishing an heir must not be spoken of lightly.

sentences.zh: 允礽為太子時，服御俱用黃色，儀注上幾於朕，實開驕縱之門。

translations.literal: When Yinreng was crown prince his apparel and equipage were all in yellow, and his ceremonial nearly equaled mine—truly opening the door to arrogance and indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: When Yinreng was crown prince his apparel and equipage were all yellow, and his ceremonial nearly equaled my own—truly opening the door to arrogance and indulgence.

sentences.zh: 宋仁宗三十年未立太子，我太祖、太宗亦未豫立。

translations.literal: Song Renzong went thirty years without establishing a crown prince; our Taizu and Taizong likewise did not establish one in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Song Renzong went thirty years without establishing a crown prince, and our Taizu and Taizong likewise did not establish one in advance.

sentences.zh: 漢、唐已事，太子幼衝，尚保無事；

translations.literal: In Han and Tang precedents, when the crown prince was young and tender, the realm still remained untroubled;
translations.idiomatic: In Han and Tang precedents, when the crown prince was young, the realm still remained untroubled;

sentences.zh: 若太子年長，左右群小結黨營私，鮮有能無過者。

translations.literal: but if the crown prince is grown, petty men at his side form factions for private gain, and few can be without fault.
translations.idiomatic: but when the crown prince is grown, petty men at his side form factions for private gain, and few escape fault.

sentences.zh: 太子為國本，朕豈不知？

translations.literal: The crown prince is the foundation of the state—do I not know this?
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is the foundation of the state—do I not know this?

sentences.zh: 立非其人，關係匪輕。

translations.literal: To establish the wrong man—the consequence is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: To establish the wrong man is no small matter.

sentences.zh: 允礽儀表、學問、才技俱有可觀，而行事乖謬，不仁不孝，非狂易而何？

translations.literal: Yinreng's bearing, learning, and talents are all commendable, yet his conduct is perverse, unkind, and unfilial—if not mania, what is it?
translations.idiomatic: Yinreng's bearing, learning, and talents are all commendable, yet his conduct is perverse, cruel, and unfilial—if not mania, what is it?

sentences.zh: 凡人幼時猶可教訓，及長而誘於黨類，便各有所為，不復能拘制矣。

translations.literal: While a man is young he may still be instructed; once grown and seduced by faction, each goes his own way and can no longer be restrained.
translations.idiomatic: While a man is young he may still be instructed; once grown and seduced by faction, each goes his own way and can no longer be restrained.

sentences.zh: 立皇太子事，未可輕定。

translations.literal: The matter of establishing a crown prince must not be lightly decided."
translations.idiomatic: The matter of establishing a crown prince must not be lightly decided."

sentences.zh: 」自是上意不欲更立太子，雖諭大學士、九卿等裁定太子儀仗，卒未用。

translations.literal: From this time the emperor's mind did not wish to establish another crown prince; although he ordered the grand secretaries and the Nine Ministers to fix the crown prince's ceremonial regalia, it was never used in the end.
translations.idiomatic: From this point the emperor did not wish to establish another crown prince. Although he ordered the grand secretaries and the Nine Ministers to fix the crown prince's ceremonial regalia, it was never used.

sentences.zh: 終清世不復立太子。

translations.literal: Throughout the Qing dynasty a crown prince was never again established.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Qing dynasty a crown prince was never again established.

sentences.zh: 五十四年十一月，有醫賀孟頫者，為允礽福金治疾，允礽以礬水作書相往來，复囑普奇舉為大將軍，事發，普奇等皆得罪。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifty-fourth year the physician He Mengfu treated Yinreng's primary consort; Yinreng used alum water to write letters back and forth, and again instructed Puqi to recommend him as commander-in-chief; when the affair came to light Puqi and others were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fifty-fourth year the physician He Mengfu treated Yinreng's primary consort. Yinreng used alum water to write secret letters back and forth and again urged Puqi to recommend him as commander-in-chief. When the plot was exposed, Puqi and the others were all punished.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，大學士王掞疏請建儲，越數日，御史陳嘉猷等八人疏繼上，上疑其結黨，疏留中不下。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year Grand Secretary Wang Yan memorialized requesting the establishment of an heir; within several days Censor Chen Jiayou and seven others submitted memorials in succession; the emperor suspected faction and retained the memorials without promulgating them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year Grand Secretary Wang Yan memorialized requesting the establishment of an heir. Within several days Censor Chen Jiayou and seven others submitted memorials in succession. The emperor suspected a faction and retained the memorials without promulgating them.

sentences.zh: 五十七年二月，翰林院檢討朱天保請復立允礽為太子，上親召詰責，辭連其父侍郎朱都納，及都統銜齊世，副都統戴保、常賚，內閣學士金寶。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifty-seventh year Hanlin Compiler Zhu Tianbao requested the restoration of Yinreng as crown prince; the emperor personally summoned and interrogated him; his words implicated his father, Vice Minister Zhu Duna, Banner General Qi Shi, Vice Banner Generals Dai Bao and Chang Ci, and Grand Secretariat Academician Jin Bao.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifty-seventh year Hanlin Compiler Zhu Tianbao requested the restoration of Yinreng as crown prince. The emperor personally summoned and interrogated him. His testimony implicated his father, Vice Minister Zhu Duna, Banner General Qi Shi, Vice Banner Generals Dai Bao and Chang Ci, and Grand Secretariat Academician Jin Bao.

sentences.zh: 朱天保、戴保誅死，朱都納及常賚、金寶交步軍統領枷示，齊世交宗人府幽禁。

translations.literal: Zhu Tianbao and Dai Bao were executed; Zhu Duna together with Chang Ci and Jin Bao were handed to the Infantry Commander for cangue display; Qi Shi was handed to the Imperial Clan Court for confinement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tianbao and Dai Bao were executed. Zhu Duna, Chang Ci, and Jin Bao were handed to the Infantry Commander for display in the cangue. Qi Shi was handed to the Imperial Clan Court for confinement.

sentences.zh: 七月，允礽福金石氏卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Yinreng's primary consort, Lady Shi, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Yinreng's primary consort, Lady Shi, died.

sentences.zh: 上稱其淑孝寬和，作配允礽，辛勤歷有年所，諭大學士等同翰林院撰文致祭。

translations.literal: The emperor praised her as virtuous, filial, generous, and gentle, having been Yinreng's consort and labored diligently for many years, and ordered the grand secretaries together with the Hanlin Academy to compose a text for the offering.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised her as virtuous, filial, generous, and gentle, having been Yinreng's consort and having served diligently for many years, and ordered the grand secretaries and the Hanlin Academy to compose a memorial text for the offering.

sentences.zh: 六十年三月，上萬壽節，掞復申前請建儲。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixtieth year, on the emperor's birthday, Yan again renewed his earlier request to establish an heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixtieth year, on the emperor's birthday, Wang Yan again renewed his earlier request to establish an heir.

sentences.zh: 越數日，御史陶彝等十二人疏繼上。

translations.literal: Within several days Censor Tao Yi and eleven others submitted memorials in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Within several days Censor Tao Yi and eleven others submitted memorials in succession.

sentences.zh: 上乃嚴旨斥掞為奸，並以諸大臣請逮掞等治罪，上令掞及彝等發軍前委署額外章京。

translations.literal: The emperor then issued a stern edict denouncing Yan as treacherous; when the grand ministers requested that Yan and the others be arrested and punished, the emperor ordered Yan and Yi and the rest dispatched to the army front as acting extra clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued a stern edict denouncing Wang Yan as treacherous. When the senior ministers requested that Yan and the others be arrested and punished, the emperor ordered Yan, Tao Yi, and the rest dispatched to the army front as acting extra clerks.

sentences.zh: 掞年老，其子奕清代行。

translations.literal: Yan was old, and his son Yiqing went in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan was elderly, and his son Yiqing went in his place.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，世宗即位，封允礽子弘晳為理郡王。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year, when the Shizong Emperor acceded, he enfeoffed Yinreng's son Hongxi as Prince Li of the Second Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year, when the Yongzheng Emperor acceded, he enfeoffed Yinreng's son Hongxi as Prince Li of the Second Rank.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，詔於祁縣鄭家莊修蓋房屋，駐劄兵丁，將移允礽往居之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng an edict ordered houses built at Zhengjiazhuang in Qi County with garrison troops stationed there, intending to move Yinreng to live there.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign an edict ordered houses built at Zhengjiazhuang in Qi County with garrison troops stationed there, intending to move Yinreng there to live.

sentences.zh: 二年十二月，允礽病薨，追封諡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year Yinreng died of illness, and a posthumous title was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year Yinreng died of illness, and a posthumous title was conferred.

sentences.zh: 六年，弘晳進封親王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Hongxi was advanced to Prince of the First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Hongxi was advanced to Prince of the First Rank.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四年十月，高宗諭責弘晳，自視為東宮嫡子，居心叵測，削爵。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Qianlong the Gaozong Emperor rebuked Hongxi for regarding himself as the legitimate son of the Eastern Palace with unfathomable intent, and stripped his title.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year of the Qianlong reign the Qianlong Emperor rebuked Hongxi for regarding himself as the legitimate son of the Eastern Palace with unfathomable intent and stripped his title.

sentences.zh: 以允礽第十子弘㬙襲郡王。

translations.literal: Yinreng's tenth son Hongdi was made to inherit as Prince of the Second Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yinreng's tenth son Hongdi inherited the title of Prince of the Second Rank.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，薨，諡曰恪。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he died; his posthumous title was Ke.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he died; his posthumous title was Ke.

sentences.zh: 子永曖，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: His son Yong'ai inherited as beile.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yong'ai inherited the title of beile.

sentences.zh: 子孫循例遞降，以輔國公世襲。

translations.literal: Descendants followed the usual rule of successive reduction in rank, with Duke of the State Assisting the Nation passing in hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants followed the usual rule of successive reduction in rank, with the title of Duke of the State Assisting the Nation passing in hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 允礽第三子弘晉、第六子弘曣、第七子弘晁、第十二子弘晥皆封輔國公。

translations.literal: Yinreng's third son Hongjin, sixth son Hongyan, seventh son Hongchao, and twelfth son Hongwan were all enfeoffed as Duke of the State Assisting the Nation.
translations.idiomatic: Yinreng's third son Hongjin, sixth son Hongyan, seventh son Hongchao, and twelfth son Hongwan were all enfeoffed as Duke of the State Assisting the Nation.

sentences.zh: 弘曣卒，諡恪僖。

translations.literal: Hongyan died; his posthumous title was Kexi.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyan died; his posthumous title was Kexi.

sentences.zh: 子永瑋，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yongwei inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongwei inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 事高宗，歷官左宗正，廣州、黑龍江、盛京將軍。

translations.literal: Serving the Gaozong Emperor, he held the posts of Left Director of the Imperial Clan, and Military Governor of Guangzhou, Heilongjiang, and Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the Qianlong Emperor, he held the posts of Left Director of the Imperial Clan and Military Governor of Guangzhou, Heilongjiang, and Mukden.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡恪勤。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Keqin.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his posthumous title was Keqin.

sentences.zh: 永曖四世孫福錕，事德宗，官至體仁閣大學士。

translations.literal: Yong'ai's fourth-generation descendant Fukun served the Dezong Emperor and rose to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Esteeming Benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Yong'ai's fourth-generation descendant Fukun served the Guangxu Emperor and rose to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Esteeming Benevolence.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡文慎。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Wenshen.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his posthumous title was Wenshen.

sentences.zh: 誠隱郡王允祉，聖祖第三子。

translations.literal: Prince Chengyin of the Second Rank Yinzhi was Shengzu's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chengyin of the Second Rank Yinzhi was Kangxi's third son.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十九年七月，偕皇太子詣古魯富爾堅嘉渾噶山行宮，上命先還。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi he went with the crown prince to the traveling palace at Gurufurjianggahunga Mountain; the emperor ordered them to return first.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-ninth year of the Kangxi reign he went with the crown prince to the traveling palace at Gurufurjianggahunga Mountain, and the emperor ordered them to return first.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，闕里孔廟成，命偕皇四子往祭。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, when the Confucian temple at Qufu was completed, he was ordered to go with the fourth prince to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year, when the Confucian temple at Qufu was completed, he was ordered to go with the fourth prince to offer sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 凡行圍、謁陵，皆從。

translations.literal: On hunts and visits to the imperial tombs he always accompanied the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On hunts and visits to the imperial tombs he always accompanied the emperor.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，上親征，允祉領鑲紅旗大營。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, when the emperor campaigned in person, Yinzhi commanded the main camp of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year, when the emperor led the campaign in person, Yinzhi commanded the main camp of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 三十七年三月，封誠郡王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirty-seventh year he was enfeoffed as Prince Cheng of the Second Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirty-seventh year he was created Prince Cheng of the Second Rank.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，敏妃之喪未百日，允祉薙髮，坐降貝勒，王府長史以下譴黜有差。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, before a hundred days had passed since Consort Min's mourning, Yinzhi shaved his head; he was demoted to beile, and the prince's mansion steward and those below were rebuked and dismissed in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year, before a hundred days had passed since Consort Min's death, Yinzhi shaved his head. He was demoted to beile, and the prince's mansion steward and those below were rebuked and dismissed in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，命勘三門底柱。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he was ordered to survey the pillars at the bottom of the Three Gates.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year he was ordered to survey the pillars at the bottom of the Three Gates.

sentences.zh: 四十六年三月，迎上幸其邸園，侍宴。

translations.literal: In the third month of the forty-sixth year he welcomed the emperor to his mansion garden and attended the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the forty-sixth year he welcomed the emperor to his mansion garden and attended the banquet.

sentences.zh: 嗣是，歲以為常，或一歲再幸。

translations.literal: Thereafter this became an annual custom, and sometimes the emperor visited twice in a year.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter this became an annual custom, and sometimes the emperor visited twice in a year.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，太子既廢，上以允祉與太子索親睦，召問太子情狀，且曰：「允祉與允礽雖暱，然未慫恿其為惡，故不罪也。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year, after the crown prince was deposed, because Yinzhi had been on intimate terms with the crown prince the emperor summoned him to question him about the crown prince's condition, and said: "Though Yinzhi was close to Yinreng, he did not urge him to do evil, and therefore is not punished."
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year, after the crown prince was deposed, the emperor summoned Yinzhi—who had been on intimate terms with the crown prince—to question him about the crown prince's conduct, and said: "Though Yinzhi was close to Yinreng, he did not urge him to do evil, and therefore is not punished."

sentences.zh: 」蒙古喇嘛巴漢格隆為允禔厭勝廢太子，允祉偵得之，發其事。

translations.literal: The Mongol Lama Bahangelong had used sorcery for Yunzhi to bring down the crown prince; Yinzhi detected it and exposed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol Lama Bahangelong had used sorcery at Yunzhi's behest to bring down the crown prince. Yinzhi detected it and exposed the affair.

sentences.zh: 明年，太子復立，允祉進封誠親王。

translations.literal: The next year, when the crown prince was restored, Yinzhi was advanced to Prince Cheng of the First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the crown prince was restored, Yinzhi was advanced to Prince Cheng of the First Rank.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，賜銀五千。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year five thousand taels of silver were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year five thousand taels of silver were bestowed on him.

sentences.zh: 聖祖邃律曆之學，命允祉率庶吉士何國宗等輯律呂、算法諸書，諭曰：「古歷規模甚好，但其數目歲久不合。

translations.literal: Shengzu was deeply versed in pitch-pipes and calendrical learning and ordered Yinzhi to lead the Hanlin bachelors He Guozong and others in compiling books on pitch-pipes and calculation, instructing: "The ancient calendar's framework is very good, but its figures after long years no longer accord.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi was deeply versed in pitch-pipes and calendrical learning and ordered Yinzhi to lead Hanlin bachelors He Guozong and others in compiling books on pitch-pipes and calculation, instructing: "The ancient calendar's framework is excellent, but its figures no longer accord after long years.

sentences.zh: 今修曆書，規模宜存古，數目宜準今。

translations.literal: In revising the calendar book now, the framework should preserve the ancient, but the figures should accord with the present."
translations.idiomatic: In revising the calendar now, the framework should preserve the ancient, but the figures should accord with the present."

sentences.zh: 五十三年十一月，書成，奏進。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifty-third year the book was completed and presented.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fifty-third year the book was completed and presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上命以律呂、曆法、算法三者合為一書，名曰《律曆淵源》。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the three—pitch-pipes, calendrical method, and calculation—combined into one book titled 《Origins of Pitch-Pipes and Calendrical Learning》.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the three—pitch-pipes, calendrical method, and calculation—combined into one book titled 《Origins of Pitch-Pipes and Calendrical Learning》.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，上有事於圜丘，拜畢，命允祉行禮。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, when the emperor performed rites at the Circular Mound Altar, after the bowing was completed he ordered Yinzhi to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year, when the emperor performed rites at the Circular Mound Altar, after the bowing was completed he ordered Yinzhi to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，封子弘晟為世子，班俸視貝子。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year his son Hongcheng was enfeoffed as heir apparent, with stipend and precedence equal to a beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year his son Hongcheng was enfeoffed as heir apparent, with stipend and precedence equal to a beizi.

sentences.zh: 六十年，上命弘晟偕皇四子、皇十二子祭盛京三陵。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year the emperor ordered Hongcheng together with the fourth prince and the twelfth prince to sacrifice at the three tombs of Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year the emperor ordered Hongcheng, together with the fourth prince and the twelfth prince, to sacrifice at the three tombs of Mukden.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，命允祉守護景陵。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor acceded he ordered Yinzhi to guard the Jing Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongzheng Emperor acceded he ordered Yinzhi to guard the Jing Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，弘晟得罪，削世子，為閑散宗室。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng Hongcheng offended and was stripped of heir-apparent status, becoming a free member of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yongzheng reign Hongcheng offended and was stripped of heir-apparent status, becoming an unattached member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 六年六月，允祉索蘇克濟賕，事發，在上前詰王大臣，上責其無臣禮，議奪爵，錮私第。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year Yinzhi demanded a bribe from Sukeji; when the affair came to light he interrogated the princes and ministers before the emperor, who rebuked him for lacking the deportment of a subject; it was deliberated to strip his title and confine him in his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the sixth year Yinzhi demanded a bribe from Sukeji. When the affair came to light he interrogated the princes and ministers before the emperor, who rebuked him for lacking the deportment of a subject. It was deliberated to strip his title and confine him in his private residence.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕止此一兄。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have only this one elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I have only this one elder brother.

sentences.zh: 朕兄弟如允祉者何限？

translations.literal: How many brothers like Yinzhi do I have?
translations.idiomatic: How many brothers like Yinzhi do I have?

sentences.zh: 皆欲激朕治其罪，其心誠不可喻。

translations.literal: All wish to provoke me to punish him—their intent truly cannot be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: All wish to provoke me into punishing him—their intent truly cannot be fathomed.

sentences.zh: 良亦朕不能感化所致，未可謂盡若輩之罪也。

translations.literal: It is also because I could not transform him by influence; one cannot say the fault lies entirely with such men."
translations.idiomatic: It is also because I could not reform him by influence; one cannot say the fault lies entirely with such men."

sentences.zh: 」命降郡王，而歸其罪於弘晟，交宗人府禁錮。

translations.literal: He was ordered reduced to Prince of the Second Rank, the guilt attributed to Hongcheng, who was handed to the Imperial Clan Court for confinement.
translations.idiomatic: He was reduced to Prince of the Second Rank, the guilt attributed to Hongcheng, who was handed to the Imperial Clan Court for confinement.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，復進封親王。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year he was again advanced to Prince of the First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year he was again advanced to Prince of the First Rank.

sentences.zh: 五月，怡親王之喪，允祉後至，無戚容。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, at Prince Yi's mourning, Yinzhi arrived late and showed no look of grief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, at Prince Yi's mourning, Yinzhi arrived late and showed no sign of grief.

sentences.zh: 莊親王允祿等劾，下宗人府議，奏稱：「允祉乖張不孝，暱近陳夢雷、周昌言，祈禳鎮魘，與阿其那、塞思黑、允禵交相黨附。

translations.literal: Prince Zhuang Yunlu and others impeached him; the case was referred to the Imperial Clan Court, which memorialized: "Yinzhi is perverse and unfilial, intimate with Chen Menglei and Zhou Changyan, prays and uses sorcery, and forms a faction with Aqina, Seshei, and Yinti.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhuang Yunlu and others impeached him. The case was referred to the Imperial Clan Court, which memorialized: "Yinzhi is perverse and unfilial, intimate with Chen Menglei and Zhou Changyan, employs prayer and sorcery, and forms a faction with Aqina, Seshei, and Yinti.

sentences.zh: 其子弘晟凶頑狂縱，助父為惡，僅予禁錮，而允祉銜恨怨懟。

translations.literal: His son Hongcheng is vicious, obstinate, and wildly unrestrained, aiding his father in evil; he was only placed in confinement, yet Yinzhi harbors resentment and rancor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongcheng is vicious, stubborn, and wildly unrestrained, aiding his father in evil. He was only placed in confinement, yet Yinzhi harbors resentment and rancor.

sentences.zh: 怡親王忠孝性成，允祉心懷嫉忌，並不懇請持服，王府齊集，遲至早散，背理蔑倫，當削爵。

translations.literal: Prince Yi was loyal and filial by nature; Yinzhi harbored jealousy, did not earnestly request to observe mourning, came late when the princes assembled at the mansion and left early—against reason and scorning propriety—and his title should be stripped."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi was loyal and filial by nature. Yinzhi harbored jealousy, did not earnestly request to observe mourning, came late when the princes assembled at the mansion and left early—against reason and scorning propriety—and his title should be stripped."

sentences.zh: 」與其子弘晟皆論死。

translations.literal: Both he and his son Hongcheng were sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Both he and his son Hongcheng were sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 上命奪爵，禁景山永安亭，聽家屬與偕，弘晟仍禁宗人府。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered his title stripped, confinement at Yong'an Pavilion on Jingshan, with family members allowed to accompany him; Hongcheng remained confined in the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his title stripped and confined him at Yong'an Pavilion on Jingshan, with family members allowed to accompany him. Hongcheng remained confined in the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 十年閏五月，薨，視郡王例殯葬。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month of the tenth year he died and was buried with the rites due a prince of the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month of the tenth year he died and was buried with the rites due a prince of the second rank.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，追諡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong a posthumous title was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Qianlong reign a posthumous title was conferred.

sentences.zh: 子弘暻，封貝子。

translations.literal: His son Hongjing was enfeoffed as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongjing was enfeoffed as beizi.

sentences.zh: 子孫遞降，以不入八分輔國公世襲。

translations.literal: Descendants followed successive reduction in rank, with Duke of the State Assisting the Nation not in the eight privileges passing in hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants followed successive reduction in rank, with the title of Duke of the State Assisting the Nation outside the eight privileges passing in hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 五世孫載齡，襲爵。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation descendant Zailing inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation descendant Zailing inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 事德宗，官至體仁閣大學士。

translations.literal: Serving the Dezong Emperor, he rose to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Esteeming Benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the Guangxu Emperor, he rose to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Esteeming Benevolence.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡文恪。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Wenke.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his posthumous title was Wenke.

sentences.zh: 恒溫親王允祺，聖祖第五子。

translations.literal: Prince Hengwen Yunqi was Shengzu's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hengwen Yunqi was Kangxi's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十五年，上征噶爾丹，命允祺領正黃旗大營。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi, when the emperor campaigned against Galdan, he ordered Yunqi to command the main camp of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year of the Kangxi reign, when the emperor campaigned against Galdan, he ordered Yunqi to command the main camp of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 四十八年十月，封恒親王。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the forty-eighth year he was enfeoffed as Prince Heng.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the forty-eighth year he was enfeoffed as Prince Heng.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，賜銀五千。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year five thousand taels of silver were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year he was granted five thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，封子弘昇為世子，班祿視貝子。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year his son Hongsheng was enfeoffed as heir apparent, with stipend and precedence equal to a beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year his son Hongsheng was enfeoffed as heir apparent, with stipend and precedence equal to a beizi.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，坐事，削世子。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, convicted of an offense, he was stripped of heir-apparent status.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Yongzheng reign, convicted of an offense, he was stripped of heir-apparent status.

sentences.zh: 十年閏五月，允祺薨，予諡。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month of the tenth year Yunqi died and was granted a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month of the tenth year Yunqi died and was granted a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 子弘晊，襲。

translations.literal: His son Hongzhi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongzhi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十年，薨，諡曰恪。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year of Qianlong he died; his posthumous title was Ke.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year of the Qianlong reign he died; his posthumous title was Ke.

sentences.zh: 子永皓，襲郡王。

translations.literal: His son Yonghao inherited as Prince of the Second Rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yonghao inherited as Prince of the Second Rank.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，薨，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year he died; his posthumous title was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year he died; his posthumous title was Jing.

sentences.zh: 弘升子永澤，襲貝子。

translations.literal: Hongsheng's son Yongze inherited as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: Hongsheng's son Yongze inherited as beizi.

sentences.zh: 子孫循例遞降，以鎮國公世襲。

translations.literal: Descendants followed the usual rule of successive reduction in rank, with Duke of the State Supporting the Nation passing in hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants followed the usual rule of successive reduction in rank, with the title of Duke of the State Supporting the Nation passing in hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 弘昇既削世子，乾隆十九年卒，予貝勒品級，諡恭恪。

translations.literal: Hongsheng, having already been stripped of heir-apparent status, died in the nineteenth year of Qianlong; he was granted beile rank and his posthumous title was Gongke.
translations.idiomatic: Hongsheng, who had already been stripped of heir-apparent status, died in the nineteenth year of the Qianlong reign. He was granted beile rank, and his posthumous title was Gongke.

sentences.zh: 淳度親王允祐，聖祖第七子。

translations.literal: Prince Chundu was Shengzu's seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chundu was Kangxi's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十五年，上征噶爾丹，命允祐領鑲黃旗大營。
