translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi, when the emperor campaigned against Galdan, he ordered Chundu to command the main camp of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year of the Kangxi reign, when the emperor campaigned against Galdan, he ordered Chundu to command the main camp of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 三十七年三月，封貝勒。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirty-seventh year he was enfeoffed as beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirty-seventh year he was enfeoffed as beile.

sentences.zh: 四十八年十月，封淳郡王。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the forty-eighth year he was enfeoffed as Prince Chun of the Second Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the forty-eighth year he was enfeoffed as Prince Chun of the Second Rank.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，賜銀五千。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year five thousand taels of silver were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year he was granted five thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 五十七年十月，正藍旗滿洲都統延信征西陲，命允祐管正藍三旗事務。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifty-seventh year, when Yanxin, Manchu Lieutenant-General of the Plain Blue Banner, campaigned on the western frontier, Chundu was ordered to administer the affairs of the three Plain Blue Banners.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fifty-seventh year, when Yanxin, Manchu Lieutenant-General of the Plain Blue Banner, campaigned on the western frontier, Chundu was ordered to administer the affairs of the three Plain Blue Banners.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，進封親王，詔褒其安分守己，敬順小心。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was advanced to Prince of the First Rank; an edict praised him for keeping to his place, being respectful and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign he was advanced to Prince of the First Rank. An edict praised him for keeping to his place and conducting himself with respectful caution.

sentences.zh: 復命與誠親王允祉並書景陵碑額，以兩王皆工書故。

translations.literal: He was again ordered, together with Prince Cheng Yinzhi, to inscribe the stele at the Jing Mausoleum, because both princes were skilled in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered, together with Prince Cheng Yinzhi, to inscribe the stele at the Jing Mausoleum, because both princes were skilled in calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，薨，予諡。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year he died and was granted a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eighth year he died and was granted a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 子弘曙。

translations.literal: His son Hongshu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Hongshu.

sentences.zh: 聖祖命皇十四子允禵為撫遠大將軍，駐甘州，令弘曙從。

translations.literal: Shengzu appointed the fourteenth prince Yinti as Grand General for the Pacification of the Distance, stationed at Ganzhou, and ordered Hongshu to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi appointed the fourteenth prince Yinti as Grand General for the Pacification of the Distance, stationed at Ganzhou, and ordered Hongshu to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 聖祖崩，世宗召還京，封世子。

translations.literal: When Shengzu died the Shizong Emperor summoned him back to the capital and enfeoffed him as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Kangxi died the Yongzheng Emperor summoned him back to the capital and enfeoffed him as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，坐事削，改封弘暻為世子。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, convicted of an offense and stripped of the title, Hongjing was instead enfeoffed as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Yongzheng reign, convicted of an offense and stripped of the title, Hongjing was instead enfeoffed as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 允祐薨，弘暻襲。

translations.literal: When Chundu died Hongjing inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Chundu died Hongjing inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十二年，薨，諡曰慎。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year of Qianlong he died; his posthumous title was Shen.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year of the Qianlong reign he died; his posthumous title was Shen.

sentences.zh: 子永鋆，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: His son Yongjun inherited as beile.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongjun inherited as beile.

sentences.zh: 子孫遞降，以鎮國公世襲。

translations.literal: Descendants followed successive reduction in rank, with Duke of the State Supporting the Nation passing in hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants followed successive reduction in rank, with the title of Duke of the State Supporting the Nation passing in hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 永鋆子綿洵，事穆宗，官涼州副都統。

translations.literal: Yongjun's son Mianxun served the Muzong Emperor and held the post of Vice Lieutenant-General of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjun's son Mianxun served the Tongzhi Emperor and held the post of Vice Lieutenant-General of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 轉戰河南、直隸、山東、湖北，克臨清，破連鎮、馮官屯，皆有功。

translations.literal: Campaigning in Henan, Zhili, Shandong, and Hubei, he captured Linqing and broke Lianzhen and Fengguantun, distinguishing himself in each action.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning in Henan, Zhili, Shandong, and Hubei, he captured Linqing and broke the defenses at Lianzhen and Fengguantun, distinguishing himself in each action.

sentences.zh: 遷荊州將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Military Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡莊武。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his posthumous title was Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 允禩，聖祖第八子。

translations.literal: Yunsi was Shengzu's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsi was Kangxi's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十七年三月，封貝勒。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirty-seventh year of Kangxi he was enfeoffed as beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirty-seventh year of the Kangxi reign he was enfeoffed as beile.

sentences.zh: 四十七年九月，署內務府總管事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the forty-seventh year he was appointed acting superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the forty-seventh year he was appointed acting superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 太子允礽既廢，允禩謀代立。

translations.literal: After Crown Prince Yinreng had been deposed, Yunsi plotted to take his place.
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Yinreng had been deposed, Yunsi plotted to take his place.

sentences.zh: 諸皇子允禟、允䄉、允禵，諸大臣阿靈阿、鄂倫岱、揆敘、王鴻緒等，皆附允禩。

translations.literal: The princes Yuntang, Yun'e, and Yinti, and the ministers Aling'a, Olonday, Kuixu, and Wang Hongxu, all supported Yunsi.
translations.idiomatic: The princes Yuntang, Yun'e, and Yinti, and the ministers Aling'a, Olonday, Kuixu, and Wang Hongxu, all supported Yunsi.

sentences.zh: 允禔言於上，謂相士張明德言允禩後必大貴，上大怒，會內務府總管凌普以附太子得罪，籍其家，允禩頗庇之，上以責允禩。

translations.literal: Yunzhi reported to the emperor that the physiognomist Zhang Mingde had said Yunsi would surely attain great eminence; the emperor was furious. At the same time Superintendent of the Imperial Household Department Ling Pu was convicted of siding with the crown prince and his property was confiscated; Yunsi had sheltered him considerably, and the emperor rebuked Yunsi.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhi reported to the emperor that the physiognomist Zhang Mingde had declared Yunsi destined for great eminence. The emperor was furious. At the same time Superintendent of the Imperial Household Department Ling Pu was convicted of siding with the crown prince and his property was confiscated. Yunsi had sheltered him at length, and the emperor rebuked Yunsi.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「凌普貪婪巨富，所籍未盡，允禩每妄博虛名，凡朕所施恩澤，俱歸功於己，是又一太子矣！

translations.literal: An edict said: "Ling Pu was greedily and enormously wealthy, and what was confiscated did not exhaust his holdings. Yunsi constantly seeks empty reputation in vain; every grace I bestow he claims credit for himself—he is another crown prince!
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Ling Pu was greedily and enormously wealthy, and what was confiscated did not exhaust his holdings. Yunsi constantly seeks empty reputation; every grace I bestow he claims for himself—he is another crown prince!

sentences.zh: 如有人譽允禩，必殺無赦。

translations.literal: If anyone praises Yunsi, he shall be put to death without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone praises Yunsi, he shall be put to death without pardon.

sentences.zh: 」翌日，召諸皇子入，諭曰：「當廢允礽時，朕即諭諸皇子有鑽營為皇太子者，即國之賊，法所不容。

translations.literal: " The next day the emperor summoned the princes in and instructed them: "When Yinreng was deposed I at once told all the princes that whoever schemed to become crown prince was a traitor to the state and would not be spared by law.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day the emperor summoned the princes and declared: "When Yinreng was deposed I at once told all the princes that whoever schemed to become crown prince was a traitor to the state and would not be spared by law.

sentences.zh: 允禩柔姦性成，妄蓄大志，黨羽相結，謀害允礽。

translations.literal: Yunsi is soft and treacherous by nature, harbors wild ambition, forms factions, and plots against Yinreng.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsi is soft and treacherous by nature, harbors wild ambition, forms factions, and plots against Yinreng.

sentences.zh: 今其事皆敗露，即鎖系，交議政處審理。

translations.literal: Now his affairs are all exposed; he is immediately placed in fetters and handed to the Deliberative Council for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Now his affairs are all exposed. He is immediately placed in fetters and handed to the Deliberative Council for trial.

sentences.zh: 」允禟語允禵，入為允禩營救，上怒，出佩刀將誅允禵；

translations.literal: " Yuntang spoke to Yinti and entered to plead for Yunsi; the emperor was enraged, drew his girdle knife, and was about to execute Yinti;
translations.idiomatic: " Yuntang spoke to Yinti and entered the palace to plead for Yunsi. The emperor was enraged, drew his girdle knife, and was about to execute Yinti;

sentences.zh: 允祺跪抱勸止，上怒少解，仍諭諸皇子、議政大臣等毋寬允禩罪。

translations.literal: Yunqi knelt and embraced him to restrain him; the emperor's anger eased somewhat, but he still instructed the princes and Deliberative Ministers not to leniently treat Yunsi's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi knelt and embraced him to restrain him. The emperor's anger eased somewhat, but he still instructed the princes and Deliberative Ministers not to leniently treat Yunsi's crime.

sentences.zh: 逮相士張明德會鞫，詞連順承郡王布穆巴，公賴士、普奇，順承郡王長史阿祿。

translations.literal: When the physiognomist Zhang Mingde was jointly tried, his testimony implicated Prince Shuncheng of the Second Rank Bumuba, Gonglaishi, Puqi, and Prince Shuncheng's chief secretary Alu.
translations.idiomatic: When the physiognomist Zhang Mingde was jointly tried, his testimony implicated Prince Shuncheng of the Second Rank Bumuba, Gonglaishi, Puqi, and Prince Shuncheng's chief secretary Alu.

sentences.zh: 張明德坐凌遲處死，普奇奪公爵，允禩亦奪貝勒，為閑散宗室。

translations.literal: Zhang Mingde was sentenced to death by lingchi; Puqi was stripped of his ducal rank; Yunsi was also stripped of beile rank and became a free member of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mingde was sentenced to death by lingchi. Puqi was stripped of his ducal rank. Yunsi was also stripped of beile rank and became an unattached member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 上復諭諸皇子曰：「允禩庇其乳母夫雅齊布，雅齊布之叔厩長吳達理與御史雍泰同榷關稅，不相能，訴之允禩，允禩借事痛責雍泰。

translations.literal: The emperor again instructed the princes: "Yunsi sheltered his wet nurse's husband Yaqibu. Yaqibu's uncle, stable chief Wudali, and Censor Yongtai jointly collected transit duties and could not get along; Wudali appealed to Yunsi, and Yunsi seized the occasion to harshly rebuke Yongtai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again instructed the princes: "Yunsi sheltered his wet nurse's husband Yaqibu. Yaqibu's uncle, stable chief Wudali, and Censor Yongtai jointly collected transit duties and could not get along. Wudali appealed to Yunsi, and Yunsi seized the occasion to harshly rebuke Yongtai.

sentences.zh: 朕聞之，以雅齊布發翁牛特公主處。

translations.literal: When I learned of it I sent Yaqibu to the territory of the Ongniot princess.
translations.idiomatic: When I learned of it I sent Yaqibu to the territory of the Ongniot princess.

sentences.zh: 允禩因怨朕，與褚英孫蘇努相結，敗壞國事。

translations.literal: Yunsi therefore resented me, joined with Sunu, grandson of Nurhaci's eldest son Cuying, and corrupted state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsi therefore resented me, joined with Sunu, grandson of Nurhaci's eldest son Cuying, and corrupted state affairs.

sentences.zh: 允禩又受制於妻，妻為安郡王岳樂甥，嫉妒行惡，是以允禩尚未生子。

translations.literal: Yunsi is also controlled by his wife; his wife is a niece of Prince An of the Second Rank Yuele, jealous and wicked in conduct, and therefore Yunsi has not yet had a son.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsi is also controlled by his wife. His wife is a niece of Prince An of the Second Rank Yuele, jealous and wicked in conduct, and therefore Yunsi has not yet had a son.

sentences.zh: 此皆爾曹所知，爾曹當遵朕旨，方是為臣子之理；

translations.literal: All this you know; you should follow my instructions—only then is the principle of subject and minister fulfilled;
translations.idiomatic: All this you know. You should follow my instructions—only then is the principle of subject and minister fulfilled;

sentences.zh: 若不如此存心，日後朕考終，必至將朕躬置乾清宮內，束甲相爭耳。

translations.literal: if you do not keep such intent in mind, after my death you will surely put my person in the Palace of Heavenly Purity and fight one another in armor.
translations.idiomatic: if you do not keep such intent in mind, after my death you will surely put my person in the Palace of Heavenly Purity and fight one another in armor.

sentences.zh: 」上幸南苑，遘疾，還宮，召允禩入見，並召太子使居咸安宮。

translations.literal: " The emperor went to the Southern Park, fell ill, returned to the palace, summoned Yunsi for an audience, and also summoned the crown prince to dwell in the Xian'an Palace.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor went to the Southern Park, fell ill, and returned to the palace. He summoned Yunsi for an audience and also had the crown prince dwell in the Xian'an Palace.

sentences.zh: 未幾，上命諸大臣於諸皇子中舉可為太子者，阿靈阿等私示意諸大臣舉允禩。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor ordered the grand ministers to name among the princes who could become crown prince; Aling'a and others privately signaled the ministers to name Yunsi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor ordered the senior ministers to name among the princes who could become crown prince. Aling'a and others privately signaled the ministers to name Yunsi.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「允禩未更事，且罹罪，其母亦微賤，宜別舉。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yunsi lacks experience in affairs, has moreover been convicted, and his mother is also of low birth; another should be chosen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Yunsi lacks experience in affairs, has moreover been convicted, and his mother is also of low birth. Another should be chosen.

sentences.zh: 」上釋允礽，亦復允禩貝勒。

translations.literal: " The emperor released Yinreng and also restored Yunsi as beile.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor released Yinreng and also restored Yunsi as beile.

sentences.zh: 四十八年正月，上召諸大臣，問倡舉允禩為太子者，諸臣不敢質言。

translations.literal: In the first month of the forty-eighth year the emperor summoned the grand ministers and asked who had advocated naming Yunsi as crown prince; the ministers did not dare speak plainly.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the forty-eighth year the emperor summoned the senior ministers and asked who had advocated naming Yunsi as crown prince. The ministers did not dare speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 上以大學士馬齊先言眾欲舉允禩，因譴馬齊，不復深詰。

translations.literal: Because Grand Secretary Ma Qi had first said the multitude wished to name Yunsi, the emperor rebuked Ma Qi and did not pursue the matter further.
translations.idiomatic: Because Grand Secretary Ma Qi had first said the multitude wished to name Yunsi, the emperor rebuked Ma Qi and did not pursue the matter further.

sentences.zh: 尋復立允礽為太子。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Yinreng was again installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yinreng was again installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 五十一年十一月，复廢允礽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifty-first year Yinreng was again deposed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fifty-first year Yinreng was again deposed.

sentences.zh: 六十一年十一月，上疾大漸，召允禩及諸皇子允祉、允祐、允禟、允䄉、允祹、允祥同受末命。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the sixty-first year, as the emperor's illness grew critical, he summoned Yunsi and the princes Yinzhi, Chundu, Yuntang, Yun'e, Yunyou, and Yinxiang together to receive his final command.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the sixty-first year, as the emperor's illness grew critical, he summoned Yunsi and the princes Yinzhi, Chundu, Yuntang, Yun'e, Yunyou, and Yinxiang together to receive his final command.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，命允禩總理事務，進封廉親王，授理籓院尚書。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor acceded he ordered Yunsi to oversee general affairs, advanced him to Prince Lian, and appointed him Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongzheng Emperor acceded he ordered Yunsi to oversee general affairs, advanced him to Prince Lian, and appointed him Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，命辦理工部事務。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was ordered to manage the affairs of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign he was ordered to manage the affairs of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 皇太子允礽之廢也，允禩謀繼立，世宗深憾之。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Yinreng was deposed, Yunsi had plotted to succeed him; the Shizong Emperor deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Yinreng was deposed, Yunsi had plotted to succeed him. The Yongzheng Emperor deeply resented this.

sentences.zh: 允禩亦知世宗憾之深也，居常怏怏。

translations.literal: Yunsi also knew how deeply the Shizong Emperor resented him and was habitually discontented.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsi also knew how deeply the Yongzheng Emperor resented him and was habitually discontented.

sentences.zh: 封親王命下，其福晉烏雅氏對賀者曰：「何賀為？

translations.literal: When the order enfeoffing him as prince of the first rank was issued, his primary consort of the Uya clan said to those offering congratulations: "What is there to congratulate?
translations.idiomatic: When the order enfeoffing him as prince of the first rank was issued, his primary consort of the Uya clan said to those offering congratulations: "What is there to congratulate?

sentences.zh: 慮不免首領耳！

translations.literal: I fear we cannot keep our heads!
translations.idiomatic: I fear we cannot keep our heads!

sentences.zh: 」語聞，世宗憾滋甚。

translations.literal: " When word reached the Shizong Emperor his resentment grew still deeper.
translations.idiomatic: " When word reached the Yongzheng Emperor his resentment grew still deeper.

sentences.zh: 會副都統祁爾薩條奏：「滿洲俗遇喪，親友饋粥吊慰。

translations.literal: It happened that Vice Lieutenant-General Qierisa memorialized: "In Manchu custom, when there is mourning friends and relatives bring congee in condolence.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Vice Lieutenant-General Qierisa memorialized: "In Manchu custom, when there is mourning friends and relatives bring congee in condolence.

sentences.zh: 後風俗漸弛，大設奢饌，過事奢靡。

translations.literal: Later the custom gradually lapsed; lavish feasts were spread and extravagance was carried too far.
translations.idiomatic: Later the custom gradually lapsed. Lavish feasts were spread and extravagance was carried too far.

sentences.zh: 」上用其議申禁，因諭斥：「允禩居母妃喪，沽孝名，百日後猶扶掖匍匐而行；

translations.literal: " The emperor adopted his proposal and issued a prohibition, then denounced: "When Yunsi was in mourning for his imperial consort mother he traded on the name of filial piety; even after the hundred days he still walked supported and crawling;
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor adopted his proposal and issued a prohibition, then denounced: "When Yunsi was in mourning for his imperial consort mother he traded on the name of filial piety. Even after the hundred days he still walked supported and crawling on the ground;

sentences.zh: 而允䄉，允禟、允指稱饋食，大肆筵席，皇考諭責者屢矣。

translations.literal: whereas Yun'e, Yuntang, and Yinti, under the pretext of bringing food in condolence, spread great banquets—the late emperor had rebuked them many times.
translations.idiomatic: whereas Yun'e, Yuntang, and Yinti, under the pretext of bringing food in condolence, spread great banquets—the late emperor had rebuked them many times.

sentences.zh: 」二年，上諭曰：「允禩素行陰狡，皇考所深知，降旨不可悉數。

translations.literal: " In the second year the emperor instructed: "Yunsi has always been secretly treacherous; the late emperor knew this thoroughly, and the edicts denouncing him cannot all be counted.
translations.idiomatic: " In the second year the emperor declared: "Yunsi has always been secretly treacherous. The late emperor knew this thoroughly, and the edicts denouncing him cannot all be counted.

sentences.zh: 自朕即位，優封親王，任以總理事務。

translations.literal: Since I acceded I have graciously enfeoffed him as prince and entrusted him with overseeing general affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Since I acceded I have graciously enfeoffed him as prince and entrusted him with overseeing general affairs.

sentences.zh: 乃不能輸其誠悃以輔朕躬，懷挾私心，至今未已。

translations.literal: Yet he cannot offer his sincere loyalty to assist me, and still harbors private intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he cannot offer his sincere loyalty to assist me and still harbors private intent.

sentences.zh: 凡事欲激朕怒以治其罪，加朕以不令之名。

translations.literal: In every matter he wishes to provoke my anger so that I may punish him and give me an ill name.
translations.idiomatic: In every matter he wishes to provoke my anger so that I may punish him and give me an ill name.

sentences.zh: 允禩在諸弟中頗有治事材，朕甚愛惜之，非允禟、允䄉等可比，是以屢加教誨，令其改過，不但成朕友於之誼，亦全前三復教誨之理？

translations.literal: Among my younger brothers Yunsi has considerable talent for governing affairs; I greatly cherish him and he is not to be compared with Yuntang, Yun'e, and the like. Therefore I have repeatedly admonished him and ordered him to reform—not only to fulfill the bond of brotherhood between us, but also to complete the principle of thrice repeated admonition?
translations.idiomatic: Among my younger brothers Yunsi has considerable talent for governing affairs. I greatly cherish him, and he is not to be compared with Yuntang, Yun'e, and the like. Therefore I have repeatedly admonished him and ordered him to reform—not only to fulfill the bond of brotherhood between us, but also to complete the principle of thrice repeated admonition?

sentences.zh: 朕一身上關宗廟社稷，不得不為？

translations.literal: My person alone bears upon the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain—I cannot but act?
translations.idiomatic: My person alone bears upon the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain—I cannot but act?

sentences.zh: 皇考慈愛之衷。

translations.literal: I must act for the late emperor's loving heart.
translations.idiomatic: I must act for the late emperor's loving intent.

sentences.zh: 朕果欲治其罪，豈有於防範。

translations.literal: If I truly wished to punish him, would there be any need for precaution?
translations.idiomatic: If I truly wished to punish him, would there be any need for precaution?

sentences.zh: 允禩在皇考時，恣意妄行，匪伊朝夕，朕可不念祖宗肇造鴻圖，以永貽子孫之安乎？

translations.literal: Under the late emperor Yunsi acted willfully and recklessly—not for a day or two. Can I fail to remember how our ancestors founded this great enterprise, so as to secure peace for posterity?
translations.idiomatic: Under the late emperor Yunsi acted willfully and recklessly—not for a day or two. Can I fail to remember how our ancestors founded this great enterprise, so as to secure peace for posterity?

sentences.zh: 三年二月，三年服滿。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year the three-year mourning period was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year the three-year mourning period was completed.

sentences.zh: 以允禩任總理事務，挾私懷詐，有罪無功，不予議敘。

translations.literal: Because Yunsi, while overseeing general affairs, harbored private intent and deceit, had guilt but no merit, he was not granted deliberative honors.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yunsi, while overseeing general affairs, harbored private intent and deceit and had guilt but no merit, he was not granted deliberative honors.

sentences.zh: 尋因工部製祈榖壇祖宗神牌草率，阿爾泰駐兵軍器粗窳，屢下詔詰責允禩；

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because the ancestral tablets for the Prayer for Grain Altar made by the Ministry of Works were careless and the garrison arms under Altai's command were crude, edicts repeatedly rebuked Yunsi;
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, because the ancestral tablets for the Prayer for Grain Altar made by the Ministry of Works were careless and the garrison arms under Altai's command were crude, edicts repeatedly rebuked Yunsi;

sentences.zh: 允禩議減內務府披甲，上令覆奏，又請一佐領增甲九十餘副。

translations.literal: Yunsi proposed reducing the armor of the Imperial Household Department; the emperor ordered a memorial in reply, and he then requested adding more than ninety sets of armor to one company.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsi proposed reducing the armor of the Imperial Household Department. The emperor ordered a memorial in reply, and he then requested adding more than ninety sets of armor to one company.

sentences.zh: 上以允禩前後異議，諭謂：「陰邪叵測，莫此為甚！

translations.literal: Because Yunsi's proposals before and after differed, an edict said: "Secretly treacherous and unfathomable—nothing surpasses this!
translations.idiomatic: Because Yunsi's proposals before and after differed, an edict declared: "Secretly treacherous and unfathomable—nothing surpasses this!

sentences.zh: 」因命一佐領留甲五十副不即裁，待缺出不補。

translations.literal: " He therefore ordered one company to retain fifty sets of armor and not cut them immediately; when vacancies occurred they would not be filled.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore ordered one company to retain fifty sets of armor and not cut them immediately; when vacancies occurred they would not be filled.

sentences.zh: 隸內務府披甲諸人集允禩邸囂閧，翌日，又集副都統李延禧家，且縱掠。

translations.literal: Those subordinate to the Imperial Household Department who wore armor gathered at Yunsi's mansion in uproar; the next day they gathered again at Vice Lieutenant-General Li Yanxi's house and even plundered freely.
translations.idiomatic: Those subordinate to the Imperial Household Department who wore armor gathered at Yunsi's mansion in uproar. The next day they gathered again at Vice Lieutenant-General Li Yanxi's house and even plundered freely.

sentences.zh: 上命捕治，諸人自列允禩使閧延禧家，允禩不置辯。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered them seized and punished; the men themselves reported that Yunsi had incited the uproar at Yanxi's house, and Yunsi offered no defense.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered them seized and punished. The men themselves reported that Yunsi had incited the uproar at Yanxi's house, and Yunsi offered no defense.

sentences.zh: 上命允禩鞫定為首者立斬，允禩以五人姓名上，上察其一乃自首，其一堅稱病未往，責允禩所讞不實。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yunsi to try and fix the ringleaders for immediate execution; Yunsi submitted five men's names; the emperor found that one had turned himself in and one steadfastly claimed illness and that he had not gone, and rebuked Yunsi's indictment as untrue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yunsi to try the ringleaders and execute them on the spot. Yunsi submitted five names, but the emperor found that one man had surrendered himself and another insisted he had been too ill to go. He rebuked Yunsi for presenting a false case.

sentences.zh: 宗人府議奪允禩爵，上命寬之。

translations.literal: The Imperial Clan Court deliberated stripping Yunsi of his title; the emperor ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Clan Court recommended stripping Yunsi of his title, but the emperor ordered leniency.

sentences.zh: 允禩杖殺護軍九十六，命太監閻倫隱其事，厚賜之。

translations.literal: Yunsi beat to death ninety-six guardsmen and ordered the eunuch Yan Lun to conceal the matter, richly rewarding him.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsi had ninety-six guardsmen beaten to death, then ordered the eunuch Yan Lun to cover it up and rewarded him handsomely.

sentences.zh: 宗人府复議奪允禩爵，上复寬之。

translations.literal: The Imperial Clan Court again deliberated stripping Yunsi of his title; the emperor again ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Clan Court again recommended stripping Yunsi of his title, and again the emperor showed leniency.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，上御西暖閣，召諸王大臣暴允禩罪狀，略曰：「當時允禩希冀非望，欲沽忠孝之名，而事事傷聖祖之心。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, the emperor held court in the West Warm Pavilion and summoned the princes and grand ministers to expose Yunsi's crimes, saying in summary: "At that time Yunsi cherished improper hopes and wished to purchase a name for loyalty and filial piety, yet in every matter he wounded Kangxi's heart.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year, the Yongzheng Emperor held court in the West Warm Pavilion and summoned the princes and senior ministers to proclaim Yunsi's crimes. He said in summary: "At that time Yunsi harbored improper ambitions and sought a reputation for loyalty and filial piety, yet in everything he did he wounded Kangxi's heart.

sentences.zh: 二阿哥坐廢，聖祖命朕與允禩在京辦事，凡有啟奏，皆蒙御批，由允禩藏貯。

translations.literal: When the second prince was deposed, Kangxi ordered me and Yunsi to manage affairs in the capital; every memorial submitted received the imperial rescript in vermilion, and Yunsi kept them in storage.
translations.idiomatic: When the second prince was deposed, Kangxi ordered me and Yunsi to manage affairs in the capital. Every memorial submitted received the emperor's vermilion rescript, and Yunsi was charged with keeping them.

sentences.zh: 嗣問允禩，則曰：'前值皇考怒，恐不測，故焚毀筆札，禦批亦納其中。

translations.literal: Later when Yunsi was questioned, he said: 'Previously, when my late father was angry, fearing the unpredictable, I therefore burned letters and papers, and the imperial rescripts were also included among them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunsi was later questioned, he said: 'When my late father was angry, I feared what might happen, so I burned the letters and papers—and the imperial rescripts were among them.

sentences.zh: '此允禩親向朕言者。

translations.literal: ' This Yunsi personally told me.
translations.idiomatic: ' This is what Yunsi personally told me.

sentences.zh: 聖祖升遐，朕念允禩夙有才幹，冀其痛改其非，為國家出力，令其總理事務，加封親王，推心置腹。

translations.literal: After Kangxi's death, remembering Yunsi's long-standing talent and ability, I hoped he would deeply reform his faults and serve the state, so I ordered him to oversee general affairs, enfeoffed him as a prince of the first rank, and treated him with complete openness.
translations.idiomatic: After Kangxi's death, I remembered Yunsi's long-standing talent and hoped he would thoroughly reform and serve the state. I put him in charge of general affairs, enfeoffed him as a prince of the first rank, and treated him with complete trust.

sentences.zh: 三年以來，宗人府及諸大臣劾議，什伯累積，朕百端容忍，乃允禩詭譎陰邪，狂妄悖亂，包藏禍心，日益加甚。

translations.literal: Over three years, impeachments and deliberations from the Imperial Clan Court and the grand ministers accumulated by tens and hundreds; I tolerated them in every way, yet Yunsi grew ever more deceitful, secretly treacherous, wildly rebellious, and harboring evil intent.
translations.idiomatic: Over three years the Imperial Clan Court and senior ministers piled up impeachments by the dozens, and I tolerated them in every way I could. Yet Yunsi grew ever more deceitful and treacherous, wildly rebellious and full of hidden malice.

sentences.zh: 朕令宗人府訊問何得將皇考禦批焚毀，允禩改言：'抱病昏昧，誤行燒毀。

translations.literal: I ordered the Imperial Clan Court to question how he could have burned my late father's imperial rescripts; Yunsi changed his account: 'While ill and confused, I mistakenly burned them.
translations.idiomatic: I ordered the Imperial Clan Court to ask how he could have burned my late father's imperial rescripts. Yunsi changed his story: 'I was ill and confused and burned them by mistake.

sentences.zh: '及朕面質之，公然設誓，詛及一家。

translations.literal: ' When I confronted him face to face, he openly swore an oath cursing the whole clan.
translations.idiomatic: ' When I confronted him directly, he openly swore an oath that cursed the entire imperial house.

sentences.zh: 允禩自絕於天，自絕於祖宗，自絕於朕，斷不可留於宗姓之內，為我朝之玷！

translations.literal: Yunsi has cut himself off from Heaven, cut himself off from the ancestors, and cut himself off from me—he absolutely cannot remain within the clan surname and become a stain upon our dynasty!
translations.idiomatic: Yunsi has cut himself off from Heaven, from the ancestors, and from me. He cannot remain within the imperial clan and become a stain on our dynasty!

sentences.zh: 謹述皇考諭，遵先朝削籍離宗之典，革去允禩黃帶子，以儆兇邪，為萬世子孫鑑戒。

translations.literal: Reverently reciting my late father's instruction, following the precedent of earlier reigns for expulsion from the register and severance from the clan, I strip Yunsi of the yellow girdle and make him a warning to the vicious and treacherous, an admonition for posterity through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: In keeping with my late father's instruction and the precedent of expulsion from the clan register, I strip Yunsi of the yellow girdle to warn the vicious and treacherous and provide a lesson for all future generations.

sentences.zh: 」並命逐其福晉還外家。

translations.literal: " He also ordered Yunsi's primary consort expelled and sent back to her natal family.
translations.idiomatic: " He also ordered Yunsi's primary consort expelled and sent back to her natal family.

sentences.zh: 二月，授允禩為民王，不留所屬佐領人員，凡朝會，視民公、侯、伯例，稱親王允禩。

translations.literal: In the second month, Yunsi was made a commoner prince; his subordinate company personnel were not retained; at all court assemblies he was treated by the precedent for commoner dukes, marquises, and earls, and addressed as Prince Yunsi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Yunsi was reduced to a commoner prince. His company personnel were removed, and at court assemblies he was treated like a commoner duke, marquis, or earl while still being addressed as Prince Yunsi.

sentences.zh: 諸王大臣請誅允禩，上不許。

translations.literal: The princes and grand ministers requested Yunsi's execution; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The princes and senior ministers asked that Yunsi be executed, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 尋命削王爵，交宗人府圈禁高牆。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered stripped of princely rank and handed to the Imperial Clan Court for confinement within the high walls.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was stripped of princely rank and handed over to the Imperial Clan Court for confinement within the high walls.

sentences.zh: 宗人府請更名編入佐領：​​允禩改名阿其那，子弘旺改菩薩保。

translations.literal: The Imperial Clan Court requested a change of name and enrollment in a company: Yunsi was renamed Aqina, and his son Hongwang was renamed Pusa Bao.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Clan Court requested that he be renamed and enrolled in a company: Yunsi was renamed Aqina, and his son Hongwang was renamed Pusa Bao.

sentences.zh: 六月，諸王大臣复臚允禩罪狀四十事，請與允禟、允並正典刑，上暴其罪於中外。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the princes and grand ministers again enumerated forty counts in Yunsi's bill of crimes and requested that he, together with Yuntang and Yinti, be punished according to law; the emperor exposed their crimes at home and abroad.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the princes and senior ministers again listed forty counts against Yunsi and asked that he, together with Yuntang and Yinti, be punished according to law. The emperor made their crimes known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 九月，允禩患嘔噦，命給與調養，未幾卒於幽所。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Yunsi suffered vomiting and hiccups; he was ordered given care and nourishment, and before long died in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Yunsi suffered vomiting and hiccups. Medical care was ordered for him, but before long he died in confinement.

sentences.zh: 諸王大臣仍請戮屍，不許。

translations.literal: The princes and grand ministers again requested posthumous mutilation; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The princes and senior ministers again asked that his corpse be mutilated, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十三年正月，高宗諭曰：「聖祖第八子允禩，第九子允禟結黨妄行，罪皆自取。

translations.literal: In the first month of the forty-third year of Qianlong, the Gaozong Emperor issued an edict saying: "Kangxi's eighth son Yunsi and ninth son Yuntang formed factions and acted recklessly; their crimes were entirely of their own making.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the forty-third year of the Qianlong reign, the Qianlong Emperor issued an edict: "Kangxi's eighth son Yunsi and ninth son Yuntang formed factions and acted recklessly. Their crimes were entirely of their own making.

sentences.zh: 皇考僅令削籍更名，以示愧辱。

translations.literal: My late father only ordered expulsion from the register and a change of name to show shame and disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: My late father only ordered them expelled from the clan register and renamed, to mark their shame and disgrace.

sentences.zh: 就兩人心術而論，覬覦窺竊，誠所不免，及皇考紹登大寶。

translations.literal: Judging the disposition of the two men, covetous watching and secret scheming were truly hard to avoid; yet once my late father succeeded to the great throne,
translations.idiomatic: Judging the two men's character, covetous ambition and secret scheming were indeed hard to avoid. Yet once my late father succeeded to the throne,

sentences.zh: 皇考晚年屢向朕諭及，愀然不樂，意頗悔？

translations.literal: in his later years my late father repeatedly spoke to me of the matter, grave and displeased, and was quite regretful?
translations.idiomatic: in his later years my late father often spoke to me of the matter, grave and unhappy, and was quite regretful?

sentences.zh: ，怨尤誹謗，亦情事所有，特未有顯然悖逆之之，若將有待。

translations.literal: Resentment, complaint, and slander were also matters to be expected, yet there were no clearly rebellious acts, as if he were waiting for something.
translations.idiomatic: Resentment and slander were also to be expected, yet there had been no clearly rebellious acts, as if he were waiting to see what might happen.

sentences.zh: 朕今臨御四十三年矣，此事重大，朕若不言，後世子孫無敢言者。

translations.literal: I have now reigned forty-three years; this matter is weighty—if I do not speak, no descendant in later ages will dare to speak.
translations.idiomatic: I have now reigned for forty-three years. This matter is too important: if I do not speak, no descendant in later ages will dare to do so.

sentences.zh: 允禩、允禟仍復原名，收入玉牒，子孫一併？

translations.literal: Yunsi and Yuntang shall have their original names restored and be entered in the imperial genealogy; their descendants shall also all?
translations.idiomatic: Yunsi and Yuntang shall have their original names restored and be entered in the imperial genealogy, and their descendants shall also all be?

sentences.zh: 入。

translations.literal: entered in the genealogy as well.
translations.idiomatic: entered in the genealogy as well.

sentences.zh: 此實仰體皇考仁心，申未竟之緒，想在天之靈​​亦當愉慰也。

translations.literal: This truly accords with my late father's benevolent heart and carries forward what he left unfinished; surely his spirit in Heaven will also be pleased and comforted.
translations.idiomatic: This truly honors my late father's benevolent intent and completes what he left unfinished. Surely his spirit in Heaven will also be pleased and comforted.

sentences.zh: 允禟，聖祖第九子。

translations.literal: Yuntang was Kangxi's ninth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuntang was Kangxi's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十七年，上責允禩，允禟語允，入為保奏，上怒。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year of Kangxi the emperor rebuked Yunsi; Yuntang spoke to Yinti and entered to intercede as guarantor; the emperor was angry.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year of the Kangxi reign the emperor rebuked Yunsi. Yuntang spoke to Yinti and entered the palace to intercede on his behalf, and the emperor was enraged.

sentences.zh: 是時，上每巡幸，輒隨。

translations.literal: At that time, whenever the emperor went on tour, he always accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time he always accompanied the emperor whenever Kangxi went on tour.

sentences.zh: 四十八年三月，封貝子。

translations.literal: In the third month of the forty-eighth year he was enfeoffed as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the forty-eighth year he was enfeoffed as beizi.

sentences.zh: 十月，命往翁牛特送和碩慍恪公主之喪。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was ordered to go to Ongniut to escort the funeral of Princess Wenke of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was ordered to go to Ongniut to escort the funeral of Princess Wenke of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，賜銀四千。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year four thousand taels of silver were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year he was granted four thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，世宗召允回京，以諸王大臣議，命允禟出駐西寧。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng the Shizong Emperor summoned Yinti back to the capital; on deliberation by the princes and grand ministers, Yuntang was ordered to go out and be stationed at Xining.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign the Yongzheng Emperor recalled Yinti to the capital. On the deliberation of the princes and senior ministers, Yuntang was ordered to take up station at Xining.

sentences.zh: 允禟屢請緩行，上譴責所屬太監，允禟行至軍。

translations.literal: Yuntang repeatedly requested delay in departure; the emperor rebuked the eunuchs under him, and Yuntang proceeded to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yuntang repeatedly asked to delay his departure. The emperor rebuked the eunuchs under him, and Yuntang eventually reached Xining.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，宗人府劾允禟擅遣人至河州買草、勘牧地，違法肆行，請奪爵，上命寬之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year the Imperial Clan Court impeached Yuntang for sending men on his own authority to Hezhou to buy fodder and survey pasture lands, acting lawlessly and wantonly, and requested stripping his title; the emperor ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year the Imperial Clan Court impeached Yuntang for sending men on his own authority to Hezhou to buy fodder and survey pasture lands in violation of the law and recommended stripping his title. The emperor ordered leniency.

sentences.zh: 三年，上聞允禟縱容家下人在西寧生事，遣都統楚宗往約束，楚宗至，允禟不出迎，傳旨詰責，曰：「上責我皆是，我復何言？

translations.literal: In the third year the emperor heard that Yuntang indulged his household servants in making trouble at Xining and dispatched the lieutenant-general Chuzong to restrain them; when Chuzong arrived, Yuntang did not come out to receive him; the transmitted edict rebuked him, saying: "The emperor's rebukes of me are all justified—what more can I say?
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the emperor heard that Yuntang was allowing his household servants to make trouble at Xining and dispatched Lieutenant-General Chuzong to restrain them. When Chuzong arrived, Yuntang did not come out to receive him. The transmitted edict rebuked him, saying: "The emperor's rebukes of me are all justified—what more can I say?

sentences.zh: 我行將出家離世！

translations.literal: I am about to leave home and quit the world!
translations.idiomatic: I am about to leave home and quit the world!

sentences.zh: 」楚宗以聞，上以允禟傲慢無人臣禮，手詔深責之，並牽連及允禩、允、允䄉私結黨援諸事。

translations.literal: " Chuzong reported this; the emperor, because Yuntang was arrogant and lacked the propriety of a subject, personally drafted an edict deeply rebuking him, and also implicated matters of Yunsi, Yinti, and Yun'e privately forming factions and mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: " Chuzong reported this. Because Yuntang was arrogant and showed none of a subject's propriety, the emperor personally drafted an edict sharply rebuking him and also raised Yunsi's, Yinti's, and Yun'e's private factional ties.

sentences.zh: 七月，山烏雅圖等經平定毆諸生，請按律治罪，陝西人稱允禟九王，為上？

translations.literal: In the seventh month Shan Wuyatu and others beat students while passing through Pingding and requested punishment according to law; people in Shaanxi called Yuntang the Ninth Prince, and this reached the emperor?
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Shan Wuyatu and others beat local students while passing through Pingding and asked that they be punished according to law. People in Shaanxi called Yuntang the Ninth Prince, and this reached the emperor?

sentences.zh: 西巡撫伊都立奏劾允禟護所聞，手詔斥為無恥，遂奪允禟爵，撤所屬佐領，即西寧幽禁，並錄允禟左右用事者毛太、佟保等，撤還京師，授以官。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi governor Yiduli memorialized impeaching Yuntang for shielding those he heard of; a personally drafted edict denounced this as shameless; Yuntang's title was then stripped, his subordinate companies withdrawn, and he was immediately confined at Xining; Mao Tai, Tong Bao, and others who wielded power at Yuntang's side were also enrolled, recalled to the capital, and given offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi governor Yiduli memorialized impeaching Yuntang for shielding those involved. A personally drafted edict denounced this as shameless. Yuntang's title was stripped, his companies withdrawn, and he was immediately confined at Xining. Mao Tai, Tong Bao, and others who wielded power at Yuntang's side were enrolled, recalled to the capital, and given official posts.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，九門捕役得毛太、佟保等寄允禟私書，以聞，上見書跡類西洋字，遣持問允禟子弘暘，弘暘言允禟所造字也。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year the Nine Gates constables obtained private letters from Mao Tai, Tong Bao, and others sent to Yuntang and reported them; the emperor saw that the script resembled Western letters and sent men to ask Yuntang's son Hongyang, who said they were characters Yuntang had invented.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year the Nine Gates constables seized private letters from Mao Tai and Tong Bao to Yuntang and reported them. The emperor saw that the script resembled Western letters and sent men to question Yuntang's son Hongyang, who said they were characters Yuntang had invented.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「從來造作隱語，防人察覺，惟敵國為然。

translations.literal: An edict said: "From antiquity the creation of secret language to keep others from detecting it has been the practice only of enemy states.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "From antiquity only enemy states have invented secret language to keep others from detecting their meaning.

sentences.zh: 允禟在西寧，未嘗禁其書札往來，何至別造字體，暗藏密遞，不可令人以共見耶？

translations.literal: Yuntang at Xining was never forbidden correspondence—why should he separately invent characters and secretly transmit messages that could not be shown openly to others?
translations.idiomatic: Yuntang at Xining was never forbidden to exchange letters—so why invent a separate script and pass secret messages that could not be shown openly?

sentences.zh: 允禟與弘暘書用朱筆，弘暘復書稱其父言為'旨'，皆僭妄非禮。

translations.literal: In letters between Yuntang and Hongyang vermilion ink was used; in Hongyang's replies he called his father's words an 'edict'—all presumptuous, reckless, and improper.
translations.idiomatic: Letters between Yuntang and Hongyang were written in vermilion ink, and in his replies Hongyang called his father's words an 'edict'—all presumptuous and improper.

sentences.zh: 允禟寄允䄉書言'事機已失'，其言尤駭人。

translations.literal: In a letter Yuntang sent to Yun'e he wrote that 'the opportunity is already lost'—those words were especially shocking.
translations.idiomatic: In a letter to Yun'e, Yuntang wrote that 'the opportunity is already lost'—words especially shocking to read.

sentences.zh: 」命嚴鞫毛太、佟保等。

translations.literal: " He ordered Mao Tai, Tong Bao, and the others strictly interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Mao Tai, Tong Bao, and the others to be strictly interrogated.

sentences.zh: 諸王大臣請治允禟罪，命革去黃帶子，削宗籍，逮還京，令胡什禮監以行。

translations.literal: The princes and grand ministers requested that Yuntang be punished; he was ordered stripped of the yellow girdle, expunged from the clan register, seized and returned to the capital, with Hushili assigned to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: The princes and senior ministers asked that Yuntang be punished. He was stripped of the yellow girdle, expunged from the clan register, seized and brought back to the capital under the escort of Hushili.

sentences.zh: 五月，令允禟改名，又以所擬字樣姦巧，下諸王大臣議，改為塞？

translations.literal: In the fifth month Yuntang was ordered to change his name; because the proposed characters were too crafty, the matter was submitted to the princes and grand ministers for deliberation, and the name was changed to Se?
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Yuntang was ordered to change his name. Because the characters he proposed were too crafty, the matter was submitted to the princes and senior ministers for deliberation, and the name was changed to Se?

sentences.zh: 楚宗及侍思黑。

translations.literal: —completing the new name Seshei.
translations.idiomatic: —completing the new name Seshei.

sentences.zh: 六月，諸王大臣复劾允禟罪狀二十八事，請誅之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the princes and grand ministers again impeached Yuntang on twenty-eight counts and requested his execution.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the princes and senior ministers again impeached Yuntang on twenty-eight counts and asked that he be executed.

sentences.zh: 胡什禮監允禟至保定，命直隸總督李紱暫禁，觀其行止。

translations.literal: Hushili escorted Yuntang to Baoding; the Zhili governor Li Fu was ordered to hold him temporarily and observe his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Hushili escorted Yuntang to Baoding. The Zhili governor Li Fu was ordered to hold him temporarily and observe his conduct.

sentences.zh: 紱語胡什禮「當便宜行事」，胡什禮以聞，上命馳諭止之，紱奏無此語。

translations.literal: Li Fu told Hushili to "act as circumstances require"; Hushili reported this; the emperor ordered a fast dispatch to stop it; Li Fu memorialized that he had said no such thing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu told Hushili to "act as circumstances require." Hushili reported this, and the emperor ordered an urgent message to stop it. Li Fu memorialized that he had said no such thing.

sentences.zh: 八月，紱奏允禟以腹疾卒於幽所。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Li Fu memorialized that Yuntang had died of abdominal illness in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Li Fu memorialized that Yuntang had died of abdominal illness in confinement.

sentences.zh: 上聞胡什禮與楚宗中途械系允禟，旋釋去，胡什禮又，乃起流言也。

translations.literal: The emperor learned that Hushili and Chuzong had shackled Yuntang midway on the route and then released him; Hushili again, and rumors arose.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor learned that Hushili and Chuzong had shackled Yuntang midway on the journey and then released him. Hushili again acted improperly, and rumors spread.

sentences.zh: 乾？

translations.literal: Qian?
translations.idiomatic: Chuzong?

sentences.zh: 妄述紱語，命並逮治。

translations.literal: He falsely reported Li Fu's words, and the emperor ordered both men seized and punished.
translations.idiomatic: He falsely reported Li Fu's words, and the emperor ordered both men seized and punished.

sentences.zh: 其後紱得罪，上猶責紱不以允禟死狀明白於隆間，復原名，還宗籍。

translations.literal: Thereafter Li Fu fell into disgrace; the emperor still rebuked him for not making Yuntang's cause of death clear in court assemblies; Yuntang's original name was restored and he was returned to the clan register.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Li Fu fell into disgrace, yet the emperor still rebuked him for not making Yuntang's cause of death clear in open court. Yuntang's original name was restored and he was returned to the clan register.

sentences.zh: 子弘晸，封不入八分輔國公，坐事奪爵。

translations.literal: His son Hongjing was enfeoffed as a fuguo gong outside the eight privileges; for an offense his title was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongjing was enfeoffed as a fuguo gong outside the eight privileges, but later lost his title for an offense.

sentences.zh: 輔國公允䄉，聖祖第十子。

translations.literal: Fuguo Gong Yun'e was Kangxi's tenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo Gong Yun'e was Kangxi's tenth son.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十八年十月，封敦郡王。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the forty-eighth year of Kangxi he was enfeoffed as Prince Dun of the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the forty-eighth year of the Kangxi reign he was enfeoffed as Prince Dun of the second rank.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，命辦理正黃旗滿洲、蒙古、漢軍三旗事。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he was ordered to manage the affairs of the Plain Yellow Banner's Manchu, Mongol, and Chinese Eight Banners.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year he was ordered to manage the affairs of the Plain Yellow Banner's Manchu, Mongol, and Chinese companies.

sentences.zh: 允䄉與允禟、允皆黨附允禩，為世宗所惡。

translations.literal: Yun'e, together with Yuntang and Yinti, all joined Yunsi's faction and were hated by the Shizong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yun'e, together with Yuntang and Yinti, all joined Yunsi's faction and were hated by the Yongzheng Emperor.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，澤卜尊丹巴胡土克圖詣京師，謁聖祖梓宮，俄病卒，上遣送靈龕還喀爾喀，命允䄉齎印冊賜奠。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng the Jebtsundamba Khutuktu came to the capital and paid respects at Kangxi's coffin palace; he soon fell ill and died; the emperor dispatched the spirit casket back to Khalkha and ordered Yun'e to carry the seal and patent to grant funeral offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign the Jebtsundamba Khutuktu came to the capital to pay respects at Kangxi's coffin palace, but soon fell ill and died. The emperor sent the spirit casket back to Khalkha and ordered Yun'e to carry the seal and patent to grant funeral offerings.

sentences.zh: 允䄉託疾不行，旋稱有旨召還，居張家口。

translations.literal: Yun'e pleaded illness and did not go; soon he claimed there was an edict recalling him and stayed at Zhangjiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Yun'e pleaded illness and did not go. Soon he claimed there was an edict recalling him and remained at Zhangjiakou.

sentences.zh: 复私行禳禱，疏文內連書「雍正新君」，為上所知，斥為不敬。

translations.literal: He again privately performed prayer and exorcism rites; in the memorial text he repeatedly wrote "the new ruler Yongzheng"; when the emperor learned of this he denounced it as disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: He again privately performed prayer and exorcism rites, and in the memorial text repeatedly wrote "the new ruler Yongzheng." When the emperor learned of this he denounced it as disrespectful.

sentences.zh: 兵部劾奏，命允禩議其罪。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War impeached and memorialized; Yunsi was ordered to deliberate his crime.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War impeached him, and Yunsi was ordered to deliberate his crime.

sentences.zh: 四月，奪爵，逮京師拘禁。

translations.literal: In the fourth month his title was stripped and he was seized and confined in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month his title was stripped and he was seized and confined in the capital.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，高宗命釋之，封輔國公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong the Gaozong Emperor ordered him released and enfeoffed as fuguo gong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Qianlong reign the Qianlong Emperor ordered him released and enfeoffed as fuguo gong.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒，詔用貝子品級祭葬。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died; an edict ordered funeral rites at beizi rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died, and an edict ordered funeral rites at beizi rank.

sentences.zh: 履懿親王允祹，聖祖第十二子。

translations.literal: Prince Luyi of the First Rank Yunyou was Kangxi's twelfth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Luyi of the First Rank Yunyou was Kangxi's twelfth son.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十八年十月，封貝子。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the forty-eighth year of Kangxi he was enfeoffed as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the forty-eighth year of the Kangxi reign he was enfeoffed as beizi.

sentences.zh: 自是有巡幸，輒從。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever there was a tour, he always accompanied.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he always accompanied the emperor whenever Kangxi went on tour.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，孝惠章皇后崩，署內務府總管事務，大事將畢，乃罷。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year, when Empress Xiaohuizhang died, he acted as commissioner of the Imperial Household Department; when the major affairs were nearly completed he was relieved.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year, when Empress Xiaohuizhang died, he served as acting commissioner of the Imperial Household Department and was relieved once the major funeral affairs were nearly complete.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，辦理正白旗滿洲、蒙古、漢軍三旗事。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he managed the affairs of the Plain White Banner's Manchu, Mongol, and Chinese Eight Banners.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year he managed the affairs of the Plain White Banner's Manchu, Mongol, and Chinese companies.

sentences.zh: 六十年，上以御極六十年，遣允祹祭盛京三陵。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year, because the emperor had reigned sixty years, Yunyou was dispatched to sacrifice at the three mausoleums of Shengjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year, marking Kangxi's sixtieth year on the throne, Yunyou was dispatched to sacrifice at the three mausoleums of Shengjing.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，授鑲黃旗滿洲都統。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year he was appointed lieutenant-general of the Bordered Yellow Banner Manchu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year he was appointed lieutenant-general of the Bordered Yellow Banner Manchu.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，進封履郡王。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor acceded he was promoted to Prince Lu of the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongzheng Emperor acceded he was promoted to Prince Lu of the second rank.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，宗人府劾允祹治事不能敬謹，請奪爵，命在固山貝子上行走。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng the Imperial Clan Court impeached Yunyou for inability to manage affairs with reverence and diligence and requested stripping his title; he was ordered to serve at gushan beizi rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yongzheng reign the Imperial Clan Court impeached Yunyou for failing to manage affairs with due reverence and diligence and recommended stripping his title. He was ordered to serve at gushan beizi rank.

sentences.zh: 二月，因聖祖配享儀注及封妃金冊遺漏舛錯，降鎮國公。

translations.literal: In the second month, because of omissions and errors in the ritual regulations for Kangxi's posthumous enshrinement and the golden patent for ennobling a consort, he was reduced to prince of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, because of omissions and errors in the ritual regulations for Kangxi's posthumous enshrinement and the golden patent for ennobling a consort, he was reduced to prince of the state.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，复封郡王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year he was again enfeoffed as prince of the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year he was again enfeoffed as prince of the second rank.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，進封履親王。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor acceded he was promoted to Prince Lu of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Emperor acceded he was promoted to Prince Lu of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十八年七月，薨，予諡。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-eighth year of Qianlong he died; a posthumous title was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-eighth year of the Qianlong reign he died, and a posthumous title was granted.

sentences.zh: 子弘昆，先卒，用世子例殯葬，餘子皆未封。

translations.literal: His son Hongkun died first and was buried by the precedent for an heir apparent; the remaining sons were none enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongkun died first and was buried by the precedent for an heir apparent. None of his remaining sons were enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 高宗命以皇四子永為允祹後，襲郡王。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor ordered the fourth imperial son Yong to become Yunyou's heir and succeed to the princedom of the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor ordered his fourth son Yonglin to become Yunyou's heir and succeed to the princedom of the second rank.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，薨，諡曰端。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he died; his posthumous title was Duan.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year he died, and his posthumous title was Duan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，追封親王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he was posthumously enfeoffed as prince of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Jiaqing reign he was posthumously enfeoffed as prince of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 子綿惠，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: His son Mianhui succeeded as beile.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mianhui succeeded as beile.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，薨，追封郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he died; he was posthumously enfeoffed as prince of the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jiaqing reign he died and was posthumously enfeoffed as prince of the second rank.

sentences.zh: 以成郡王綿懃子奕綸為後，襲貝子，進貝勒。

translations.literal: Mianqin's son Yilun of Prince Cheng of the second rank was made heir; he succeeded as beizi and was promoted to beile.
translations.idiomatic: Yilun, son of Prince Cheng of the second rank Mianqin, was made heir. He succeeded as beizi and was later promoted to beile.

sentences.zh: 子孫循例遞降，以鎮國公世襲。

translations.literal: Descendants successively declined by precedent, with prince of the state passing in perpetual inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants successively declined by precedent, with the title of prince of the state passing in perpetual inheritance.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十二年，高宗南巡，還蹕次涿州，有僧攜童子迎駕，自言永庶子，為側室福晉王氏所棄，僧育以長。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year of Qianlong, during the Gaozong Emperor's southern tour, on the return halt at Zhuozhou a monk brought a boy to greet the imperial procession, saying he was Yong's son by a concubine, abandoned by the secondary consort fujin of the Wang clan and raised by the monk.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year of the Qianlong reign, during the Qianlong Emperor's southern tour, on the return halt at Zhuozhou a monk brought a boy to greet the imperial procession. The boy claimed to be Yonglin's son by a concubine, abandoned by secondary consort Wang and raised by the monk.

sentences.zh: 上問永嫡福晉伊爾根覺羅氏，言永子以痘殤。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Yong's primary consort of the Irgen Gioro clan, who said Yong's son had died young of smallpox.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Yonglin's primary consort, née Irgen Gioro, who said Yonglin's son had died young of smallpox.

sentences.zh: 乃令入都，命軍機大臣詰之。

translations.literal: He was therefore ordered to enter the capital, and the Grand Council ministers were commanded to interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: The boy was therefore ordered to enter the capital, and the Grand Council ministers were commanded to interrogate him.

sentences.zh: 童子端坐名諸大臣，諸大臣不敢決。

translations.literal: The boy sat upright and called the grand ministers by name; the grand ministers did not dare decide.
translations.idiomatic: The boy sat upright and called the senior ministers by name, and the ministers did not dare reach a decision.

sentences.zh: 軍機章京保成直前批其頰，叱之，童子乃自承劉氏子，僧教為妄語。

translations.literal: Grand Council clerk Baocheng stepped forward and struck his cheek, rebuking him; the boy then confessed of his own accord that he was a Liu clansman's son, and that the monk had taught him to speak falsely.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Council clerk Baocheng stepped forward, slapped the boy's cheek, and rebuked him. The boy then admitted on his own that he was a Liu clansman's son and that the monk had coached him to lie.

sentences.zh: 斬僧，戍童子伊犁，仍自稱皇孫，所為多不法。

translations.literal: The monk was beheaded; the boy was banished to Ili; he still called himself an imperial grandson, and his conduct was largely unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: The monk was beheaded and the boy was banished to Ili. He continued to call himself an imperial grandson and behaved in many unlawful ways.

sentences.zh: 上命改戍黑龍江，道庫倫，庫倫辦事大臣松筠責其不法，縛出，絞殺之，高宗嘉其明決。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered his banishment changed to Heilongjiang; passing through Khüree, the Khüree commissioner Songyun rebuked his unlawfulness, bound him and led him out, and had him strangled; the Gaozong Emperor praised his clear decisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that he be banished to Heilongjiang instead. Passing through Khüree, Commissioner Songyun rebuked his misconduct, had him bound and taken out, and executed him by strangulation. The Qianlong Emperor praised Songyun's firm and decisive action.

sentences.zh: 怡賢親王允祥，聖祖第十三子。

translations.literal: Prince Yixian of the First Rank Yunxiang was Kangxi's thirteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yixian of the First Rank Yunxiang was Kangxi's thirteenth son.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十七年，從上謁陵。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year of Kangxi he accompanied the emperor to pay respects at the mausoleums.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year of the Kangxi reign he accompanied the emperor to pay respects at the imperial mausoleums.

sentences.zh: 自是有巡幸，輒從。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever there was an imperial tour, he always accompanied.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he always accompanied the emperor whenever Kangxi went on tour.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，世宗即位，封為怡親王。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year, when the Shizong Emperor acceded, he was enfeoffed as Prince Yi of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year, when the Yongzheng Emperor acceded, he was enfeoffed as Prince Yi of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 尋命總理戶部三庫。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to oversee the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to oversee the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，命總理戶部。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was ordered to oversee the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongzheng reign he was ordered to oversee the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十一月，諭：「怡親王於皇考時敬謹廉潔，家計空乏，舉國皆知。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month an edict said: "Prince Yi in my late father's time was reverent, diligent, and incorrupt; his household was destitute, and the whole realm knew it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Yongzheng Emperor proclaimed: "In my late father's time Prince Yi was reverent, diligent, and incorrupt. His household was destitute, and the whole realm knew it.

sentences.zh: 朕御極以來，一心翊戴，克盡臣弟之道。

translations.literal: Since I ascended the throne he has devoted himself to supporting me and fully fulfilled the way of a younger brother and subject.
translations.idiomatic: Since I ascended the throne he has devoted himself to supporting me and fully lived up to his duties as both younger brother and subject.

sentences.zh: 從前兄弟分封，各得錢糧二十三萬兩，朕援此例賜之，奏辭不已，宣諭再四，僅受十三萬；

translations.literal: When brothers were enfeoffed in the past each received 230,000 taels of stipend; I applied this precedent to grant it to him; he memorialized refusing without end; after repeated edicts he accepted only 130,000;
translations.idiomatic: When my brothers were enfeoffed in the past each received 230,000 taels of stipend. I applied that precedent in granting to him, but he memorialized again and again refusing. After repeated proclamations he accepted only 130,000 taels;

sentences.zh: 复援裕親王例，令支官物六年，王又固辭。

translations.literal: I again applied the precedent of Prince Yu, ordering supplies of official goods for six years, and the prince again steadfastly declined.
translations.idiomatic: I also applied the precedent of Prince Yu, allowing him official supplies for six years, but the prince again steadfastly declined.

sentences.zh: 今不允所請，既不可；

translations.literal: Now if I do not grant his request, that will not do;
translations.idiomatic: If I now refuse his request, that will not do;

sentences.zh: 允其請，而實心為國之懿親，轉不得與諸弟兄比，朕心不安。

translations.literal: yet if I grant his request, a kinsman who truly serves the state with all his heart will instead be unable to compare with his brothers, and my heart is uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: yet if I grant his request, a kinsman who truly serves the state with all his heart will be unable to receive what my other brothers did, and that weighs on my conscience.

sentences.zh: 」下諸王大臣議。

translations.literal: " He submitted the matter to the princes and grand ministers for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " He submitted the matter to the princes and senior ministers for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 既，仍允王請，命王所兼管佐領俱為王一等一員、二等四員、三等十二員，豹尾槍二、長桿刀二，每佐領增親軍二名？

translations.literal: Thereafter the prince's request was still granted; all companies under the prince's joint management were made his retainers, with one first-rank guard, four second-rank, twelve third-rank, two leopard-tail spears, two long-shafted blades, and two personal guards added to each company.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the prince's request was still granted. All companies under his joint management were assigned as his retainers, with enhanced guard ranks—one first-rank guard, four second-rank, twelve third-rank, two leopard-tail spears, two long-shafted blades, and two personal guards added to each company.

sentences.zh: 屬，加護。

translations.literal: They were assigned as retainers with enhanced guard protection.
translations.idiomatic: They were assigned as retainers with enhanced guard protection.

sentences.zh: 二年，允祥請除加色、加平諸弊，並增設三庫主事、庫大使，從之。

translations.literal: In the second year Yunxiang requested the abolition of the abuses of added surcharges and added balance adjustments, and the addition of director and warehouse superintendent posts in the three treasuries; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Yunxiang requested the abolition of surcharge and balance-padding abuses and the addition of director and warehouse superintendent posts in the three treasuries, and his request was approved.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，三年服滿。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year the three-year mourning period ended.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year the three-year mourning period ended.

sentences.zh: 以王總理事務謹慎忠誠，從優議敘，復加封郡王，任王於諸子？

translations.literal: Because the prince had managed affairs with caution, loyalty, and fidelity, he was given preferential commendation, again enfeoffed as prince of the second rank, and allowed among his sons to choose by finger-pointing for enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Because the prince had managed affairs with caution and steadfast loyalty, he was given preferential commendation, promoted again to prince of the second rank, and permitted to designate one of his sons for enfeoffment by pointing.

sentences.zh: 中指封。

translations.literal: He was permitted to designate an heir by pointing among his sons.
translations.idiomatic: He was permitted to designate an heir by pointing among his sons.

sentences.zh: 八月，加俸銀萬。

translations.literal: In the eighth month an additional stipend of ten thousand taels of silver was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was granted an additional stipend of ten thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 京畿被水，命往勘。

translations.literal: When the capital region was flooded he was ordered to go and inspect.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital region suffered flooding he was ordered to go and inspect the damage.

sentences.zh: 十二月，令總理京畿水利。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was ordered to oversee water conservancy in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was ordered to oversee water conservancy throughout the capital region.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「直隸河與汶河合流東下。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The Wei River joins the Wen River and flows eastward.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The Wei River joins the Wen River and flows eastward.

sentences.zh: 滄、景以下，春？

translations.literal: Below Cangzhou and Jingzhou, in the spring flood season,
translations.idiomatic: Below Cangzhou and Jingzhou, during the spring flood season,

sentences.zh: 河、淀河、子牙河、永定河皆匯於天津大直沽入海，河？

translations.literal: the Wei River, the Dian River, the Ziya River, and the Yongding River all gather at Dazhigu in Tianjin to enter the sea; the river channels
translations.idiomatic: the Wei River, the Dian River, the Ziya River, and the Yongding River all gather at Dazhigu in Tianjin to enter the sea. The channels

sentences.zh: 多淺阻，伏秋暴漲，不免潰溢。

translations.literal: are largely shallow and obstructed; in summer and autumn sudden floods inevitably burst the banks.
translations.idiomatic: are largely shallow and obstructed, and when summer and autumn floods surge the banks inevitably overflow.

sentences.zh: 請將滄州磚河、青縣興濟河故道疏濬，築減水壩，以洩之漲；

translations.literal: I request dredging the old channels of the Brick River at Cangzhou and the Xingji River at Qingxian, building spillway dams to discharge flood waters;
translations.idiomatic: He requested dredging the old channels of the Brick River at Cangzhou and the Xingji River at Qingxian and building spillway dams to discharge floodwaters;

sentences.zh: 並於白塘口入海處開直河，使磚河、興濟河同歸白塘出海；

translations.literal: and at the Baitang estuary where the rivers enter the sea opening a straight channel so the Brick River and Xingji River together return to Baitang to reach the sea;
translations.idiomatic: and opening a straight channel at the Baitang estuary so the Brick River and Xingji River could together reach the sea through Baitang;

sentences.zh: 又濬東、西二淀，多開引河，使脈絡相通，溝澮四達；

translations.literal: also dredging the eastern and western marshes, opening many diversion channels so the water network connects and drains reach in all directions;
translations.idiomatic: also dredging the eastern and western marshes, opening diversion channels so the waterways connected and drains reached in all directions;

sentences.zh: 仍疏趙北、苑家二口以防衝決。

translations.literal: still clearing the Zhao North and Yuanjia outlets to guard against breach and collapse.
translations.idiomatic: and still clearing the Zhao North and Yuanjia outlets to guard against breaches.

sentences.zh: 子牙河為滹沱及漳水下流，其下有清河、夾河、月河同趨於淀，宜開決分注，緩其奔放之勢。

translations.literal: The Ziya River is the lower course of the Hutuo and Zhang Rivers; below it the Qing, Jia, and Yue rivers together trend toward the marshes; outlets should be opened to divide the flow and slow its rushing force.
translations.idiomatic: The Ziya River carries the lower courses of the Hutuo and Zhang Rivers. Below it the Qing, Jia, and Yue rivers all trend toward the marshes, so outlets should be opened to divide the flow and slow its force.

sentences.zh: 永定河故道已湮，應自柳義水所歸，應逐年疏濬，使濁水不能為患。

translations.literal: The Yongding River's old channel was already silted up; from Liuyi Kou the waters should be drawn, and it should be dredged year by year so muddy water cannot become a hazard.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongding River's old channel was already silted up. From Liuyi Kou the waters should be drawn and dredged year by year so muddy water could no longer become a hazard.

translations.literal: The channel should be drawn slightly north from the outlet,
translations.idiomatic: The channel should be drawn slightly north from Liuyi Kou,

sentences.zh: 口引之稍北，繞王慶坨東北入淀，至三角淀，為又請於京東灤、薊、天津，京南文、霸、任丘、新、雄諸州縣設營田專官，募農耕種。

translations.literal: circling northeast of Wangqingtuo to enter the marshes, reaching Triangular Marsh, where all waters gather; he also requested in eastern Jingdong at Luan, Ji, and Tianjin, and in southern Jingnan at Wen, Ba, Renqiu, Xin, and Xiong counties and prefectures the appointment of special farm-colony officials to recruit farmers for cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: circling northeast of Wangqingtuo to enter the marshes and reach Triangular Marsh, where all waters gather. He also requested special farm-colony officials in eastern Jingdong at Luan, Ji, and Tianjin and in southern Jingnan at Wen, Ba, Renqiu, Xin, and Xiong to recruit farmers for cultivation.

sentences.zh: 」四年二月，疏言直隸興修水利，請分諸河為四局，下吏、工諸部議，議以南運河與臧家橋以下之子牙河、苑家口以東之淀河為一局，令天津道領之；

translations.literal: " In the second month of the fourth year he memorialized on waterworks in Zhili, requesting that the rivers be divided into four bureaus; the matter was submitted to the Ministries of Personnel and Works for deliberation; they decided that the Grand Canal south of Zangjia Bridge together with the Ziya River below it and the Dian River east of Yuanjiakou would form one bureau under the Tianjin intendant;
translations.idiomatic: " In the second month of the fourth year he memorialized on waterworks in Zhili and requested that the rivers be divided into four bureaus. The Ministries of Personnel and Works deliberated and decided that the Grand Canal south of Zangjia Bridge, the Ziya River below it, and the Dian River east of Yuanjiakou would form one bureau under the Tianjin intendant;

sentences.zh: 苑家口以西各淀池及畿南諸河為一局，以大名道改清河道領之；

translations.literal: the marshes west of Yuanjiakou and the southern capital-region rivers would form one bureau, with the Daming intendant changed to Qinghe intendant to lead it;
translations.idiomatic: the marshes west of Yuanjiakou and the southern capital-region rivers would form one bureau, led by the Daming intendant retitled Qinghe intendant;

sentences.zh: 永定河為一局，以永定分司改道領之；

translations.literal: the Yongding River would form one bureau, with the Yongding sub-commissioner changed to intendant to lead it;
translations.idiomatic: the Yongding River would form one bureau, led by the Yongding sub-commissioner promoted to intendant;

sentences.zh: 北運河為一局，撤分司以通永道領之：分隸專官管轄。

translations.literal: the Northern Grand Canal would form one bureau, with the sub-commissioner withdrawn and the Tongyong intendant leading it: each placed under specialized officials for jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: and the Northern Grand Canal would form one bureau, with the sub-commissioner withdrawn and the Tongyong intendant placed in charge—each under a specialized official.

sentences.zh: 尋又命分設京東、京西水利營田使各一。

translations.literal: Soon separate eastern Jingdong and western Jingxi water-conservancy and farm-colony commissioners were also appointed, one each.
translations.idiomatic: Soon separate eastern Jingdong and western Jingxi water-conservancy and farm-colony commissioners were also appointed.

sentences.zh: 三月，疏陳京東水利諸事。

translations.literal: In the third month he memorialized on waterworks affairs in eastern Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he memorialized on waterworks affairs in eastern Jingdong.

sentences.zh: 五月，疏陳畿輔西南水利諸事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he memorialized on waterworks affairs in southwestern Jifu.
