translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he memorialized on waterworks affairs in southwestern Jifu.

sentences.zh: 皆下部議行。

translations.literal: All were submitted to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All were submitted to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 七月，賜御書「忠敬誠直勤慎廉明」榜，諭曰：「怡親王事朕，克殫忠誠，職掌有九，而公爾忘私，視國如家，朕深知王德，覺此八字無一毫過量之詞。

translations.literal: In the seventh month an imperial inscription reading "Loyal, reverent, sincere, upright, diligent, cautious, incorrupt, and clear-sighted" was bestowed; an edict said: "Prince Yi serves me with complete loyalty; he holds nine offices yet forgets private interest for public duty and treats the state as his own household. I know the prince's virtue deeply and feel these eight characters contain not one word of excess praise.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Yongzheng Emperor bestowed an imperial inscription reading "Loyal, reverent, sincere, upright, diligent, cautious, incorrupt, and clear-sighted" and proclaimed: "Prince Yi serves me with complete loyalty. He holds nine offices yet forgets private interest for public duty and treats the state as his own household. I know the prince's character well and feel these eight words contain not a trace of excess praise.

sentences.zh: 在朝諸臣，於'忠勤慎明'尚多有之，若'敬誠直廉'，則未能輕許。

translations.literal: Among the ministers at court, many can still be found for 'loyal, diligent, cautious, and clear-sighted,' but for 'reverent, sincere, upright, and incorrupt' one cannot lightly grant the title.
translations.idiomatic: Among the ministers at court, many can still be found for 'loyal, diligent, cautious, and clear-sighted,' but for 'reverent, sincere, upright, and incorrupt' the title cannot lightly be granted.

sentences.zh: 期咸砥礪，以副朕望。

translations.literal: I expect all to refine themselves to fulfill my hopes.
translations.idiomatic: I expect all to refine themselves to fulfill my hopes.

sentences.zh: 」七年六月，命辦理西北兩路軍​​機。

translations.literal: " In the sixth month of the seventh year he was ordered to manage military affairs on the northwestern and southwestern routes.
translations.idiomatic: " In the sixth month of the seventh year he was ordered to manage military affairs on the northwestern and southwestern routes.

sentences.zh: 十月，命增儀仗一倍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was ordered to double his ceremonial guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was ordered to double his ceremonial guard.

sentences.zh: 十一月，王有疾。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the prince fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the prince fell ill.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，疾篤，上親臨視，及至，王已薨，上悲慟，輟朝三日。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year, when his illness was grave, the emperor came in person to visit; by the time he arrived the prince had already died; the emperor grieved deeply and suspended court for three days.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year, when his illness turned grave, the Yongzheng Emperor came in person to visit him. By the time he arrived the prince had already died. The emperor grieved deeply and suspended court for three days.

sentences.zh: 翌日，上親臨奠，諭：「怡親王薨逝，中心悲慟，飲食無味，寢臥不安。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor came in person to offer sacrifice and proclaimed: "Prince Yi has passed away; my heart grieves deeply; food has no flavor and sleep brings no rest.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Yongzheng Emperor came in person to offer sacrifice and proclaimed: "Prince Yi has passed away. My heart grieves deeply; food has no flavor and sleep brings no rest.

sentences.zh: 王事朕八年如一日，自古無此公忠體國之賢王，朕待王亦宜在常例之外。

translations.literal: The prince served me for eight years as though each day were the first; since antiquity there has never been such a worthy prince who served the state with public loyalty; my treatment of the prince should also have been beyond ordinary precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The prince served me for eight years as though each day were the first. Since antiquity there has never been such a worthy prince who served the state with public loyalty, and my treatment of him should also have gone beyond ordinary precedent.

sentences.zh: 今朕素服一月，諸臣常服，宴會俱不必行。

translations.literal: Now I shall wear plain mourning for one month; the ministers shall wear ordinary dress, and banquets need not be held.
translations.idiomatic: Now I shall wear plain mourning for one month. The ministers shall wear ordinary dress, and banquets need not be held.

sentences.zh: 」越日，复諭舉怡親王功德，命復其名上一字為「胤」，配享太廟，諡曰賢，並以「忠敬誠直勤慎廉明」八字加於諡上。

translations.literal: " The next day he again proclaimed the prince's merits and ordered the first character of his name restored to "Yin," enshrinement in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, a posthumous title of Xian, and the eight characters "Loyal, reverent, sincere, upright, diligent, cautious, incorrupt, and clear-sighted" added to the posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day he again proclaimed the prince's merits and ordered the first character of his name restored to "Yin," enshrinement in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, a posthumous title of Xian, and the eight words "Loyal, reverent, sincere, upright, diligent, cautious, incorrupt, and clear-sighted" added to the posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 白家甿等十三村民請建祠，允之。

translations.literal: Villagers of Baijiatuan and twelve other villages requested a temple be built; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers of Baijiatuan and twelve other villages requested that a temple be built in his honor, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 撥官地三十餘頃為祭田，免租賦。

translations.literal: More than thirty qing of official land was allocated as sacrificial fields, exempt from rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty qing of official land was allocated as sacrificial fields, exempt from rent and tax.

sentences.zh: 命更定園寢之制，視常例有加。

translations.literal: The regulations for the princely tomb precinct were revised, with additions beyond ordinary precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The regulations for the princely tomb precinct were revised with additions beyond ordinary precedent.

sentences.zh: 又命未殯，月賜祭；

translations.literal: He also ordered that before burial monthly sacrifices be granted;
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered that before burial monthly sacrifices be granted;

sentences.zh: 小祥及殯，視大祭禮賜祭；

translations.literal: at the small anniversary and burial, sacrifices be granted on the scale of the great sacrificial rites;
translations.idiomatic: at the small anniversary and burial, sacrifices be granted on the scale of the great sacrificial rites;

sentences.zh: 三年後，歲賜祭。

translations.literal: after three years, annual sacrifices be granted.
translations.idiomatic: after three years, annual sacrifices be granted.

sentences.zh: 皆特恩，不為例。

translations.literal: All were special favors and not made precedent.
translations.idiomatic: All were special favors and were not made precedent.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，祀盛京賢王祠。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong reign he was enshrined in the Worthy Princes Temple at Shengjing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianlong reign he was enshrined in the Worthy Princes Temple at Shengjing.

sentences.zh: 命王爵世襲。

translations.literal: The prince's title was ordered to pass in perpetual inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's title was ordered to pass in perpetual inheritance.

sentences.zh: 子弘曉，襲。

translations.literal: His son Hongxiao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongxiao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十三年，薨，諡曰僖。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year of Qianlong he died; his posthumous title was Xi.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year of the Qianlong reign he died, and his posthumous title was Xi.

sentences.zh: 子永瑯，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yonglang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yonglang succeeded.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，薨，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he died; his posthumous title was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Jiaqing reign he died, and his posthumous title was Gong.

sentences.zh: 孫奕勳，襲。

translations.literal: His grandson Yixun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yixun succeeded.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，薨，諡曰恪。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he died; his posthumous title was Ke.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he died, and his posthumous title was Ke.

sentences.zh: 子載坊，襲。

translations.literal: His son Zaifang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zaifang succeeded.

sentences.zh: 明年，薨。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he died.

sentences.zh: 弟載垣，襲。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zaituan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zaituan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 事宣宗，命在御大臣。

translations.literal: Serving the Daoguang Emperor, he was ordered to serve as an imperial front-rank grand minister.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the Daoguang Emperor, he was ordered to serve as an imperial front-rank grand minister.

sentences.zh: 咸豐八年，賜紫禁城內肩？

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xianfeng he was granted the use of a shoulder sedan within the Forbidden City.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Xianfeng reign he was granted the use of a shoulder sedan within the Forbidden City.

sentences.zh: 前大臣行走，受顧命。

translations.literal: He served as a front-rank grand minister and received the imperial deathbed testament.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a front-rank grand minister and received the imperial deathbed testament.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，歷左宗正、宗令、領侍輿。

translations.literal: When the Wenzong Emperor acceded he successively held the posts of Left Director of the Imperial Clan, Director of the Imperial Clan, and Chief Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianfeng Emperor acceded he successively held the posts of Left Director of the Imperial Clan, Director of the Imperial Clan, and Chief Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 載垣與鄭王端華及端華弟肅順皆為上所倚，相結，權勢日張。

translations.literal: Zaituan, together with Prince Zheng Duanhua and Duanhua's younger brother Sushun, were all relied upon by the emperor; they formed a faction and their power grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Zaituan, together with Prince Zheng Duanhua and Duanhua's younger brother Sushun, were all favorites of the emperor. They formed a faction and their power grew daily.

sentences.zh: 九年，命赴天津察視海防。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was ordered to go to Tianjin to inspect coastal defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was ordered to go to Tianjin to inspect coastal defenses.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，萬壽節，賜杏黃色端罩。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, on the Longevity Festival, an apricot-yellow formal surcoat was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year, on the Longevity Festival, he was bestowed an apricot-yellow formal surcoat.

sentences.zh: 七月，英吉利、法蘭西兩國兵至天津，命與兵部尚書穆廕以欽差大臣赴通州與英人議和。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, when English and French troops reached Tianjin, he was ordered with Minister of War Muyin to go as imperial commissioners to Tongzhou to negotiate peace with the English.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, when English and French troops reached Tianjin, he was ordered with Minister of War Muyin to go as imperial commissioners to Tongzhou to negotiate peace with the English.

sentences.zh: 時大學士桂良已於天津定議，上許英使額爾金至通州簽約，英使額爾金請入京師親遞國書，不許。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Secretary Guiliang had already settled terms at Tianjin; the emperor permitted the English envoy Elgin to come to Tongzhou to sign the treaty; the English envoy Elgin requested to enter the capital to deliver the letter of credence in person; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Grand Secretary Guiliang had already settled terms at Tianjin. The emperor permitted the English envoy Elgin to come to Tongzhou to sign the treaty, but when Elgin requested to enter the capital to deliver the letter of credence in person the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 兵復進，上以和議未成，罷載垣欽差大臣。

translations.literal: The troops advanced again; because the peace talks were not completed the emperor dismissed Zaituan as imperial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The troops advanced again. Because the peace talks were not completed the emperor dismissed Zaituan as imperial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未幾，扈上幸熱河。

translations.literal: Before long he accompanied the emperor on the journey to Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he accompanied the emperor on the journey to Rehe.

sentences.zh: 及和議定，？

translations.literal: When the peace agreement was settled, the ministers requested return to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: When the peace agreement was settled, the ministers requested return to the capital,

sentences.zh: 臣請還京師，上猶豫未決。

translations.literal: the emperor hesitated and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: but the emperor hesitated and had not decided.

sentences.zh: 十一年七月，文宗崩，穆宗即位，載垣等受遺詔輔政，與端華、景壽、肅順及軍機大臣穆廕、匡源、杜翰、焦祐瀛稱「贊襄政務王大臣」，擅政。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eleventh year the Wenzong Emperor died and the Muzong Emperor acceded; Zaituan and the others received the deathbed testament to assist in government; together with Duanhua, Jingshou, Sushun, and the Grand Council ministers Muyin, Kuang Yuan, Du Han, and Jiao Youying they styled themselves "Grand Ministers Assisting in Government" and monopolized power.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eleventh year the Xianfeng Emperor died and the Tongzhi Emperor acceded. Zaituan and the others received the deathbed testament to assist in government. Together with Duanhua, Jingshou, Sushun, and the Grand Council ministers Muyin, Kuang Yuan, Du Han, and Jiao Youying they styled themselves "Grand Ministers Assisting in Government" and monopolized power.

sentences.zh: 九月，上奉文宗喪還京師，詔罪狀載垣等，奪爵職，下王大臣按治，議殊死，賜自盡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, as the emperor accompanied the Wenzong Emperor's funeral back to the capital, an edict proclaimed the crimes of Zaituan and the others, stripped their titles and offices, and submitted them to princes and ministers for investigation; death by dismemberment was recommended and self-strangulation was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, as the emperor accompanied the Xianfeng Emperor's funeral back to the capital, an edict proclaimed the crimes of Zaituan and the others, stripped their titles and offices, and submitted them to princes and ministers for investigation. Death by dismemberment was recommended and self-strangulation was granted.

sentences.zh: 事詳肅順傳。

translations.literal: The affair is detailed in the biography of Sushun.
translations.idiomatic: The affair is detailed in the biography of Sushun.

sentences.zh: 爵降為不入八分輔國公，並命不得以其子孫及親兄弟子承襲。

translations.literal: The title was reduced to fuguo gong outside the eight privileges, and an order was issued that neither his descendants nor the sons of his close brothers might succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The title was reduced to fuguo gong outside the eight privileges, and an order was issued that neither his descendants nor the sons of his close brothers might succeed.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，以莊親王允祿四世孫載泰襲輔國公，收府第敕書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Zaitai, fourth-generation descendant of Prince Zhuang Yunlu, succeeded as fuguo gong, and the princely residence patent was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign Zaitai, fourth-generation descendant of Prince Zhuang Yunlu, succeeded as fuguo gong, and the princely residence patent was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，師克江寧，推恩還王爵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year, when the army captured Jiangning, favor was extended and the princely title was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year, when the army captured Jiangning, favor was extended and the princely title was restored.

sentences.zh: 九月，以寧郡王弘？

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Zaidun, fourth-generation descendant of Prince Ning Hongjiao and prince of the state, succeeded as Prince Yi,
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Zaidun, fourth-generation descendant of Prince Ning Hongjiao and prince of the state, succeeded as Prince Yi,

sentences.zh: 四世孫鎮國公載敦襲怡親王，還敕書。

translations.literal: and the patent was restored.
translations.idiomatic: and the patent was restored.

sentences.zh: 光緒十六年，薨，諡，奪爵，以先薨免罪。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Guangxu he died; a posthumous title was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of the Guangxu reign he died, and a posthumous title was granted.

sentences.zh: 弟之？

translations.literal: His posthumous title
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title

sentences.zh: 曰端。

translations.literal: was Duan.
translations.idiomatic: was Duan.

sentences.zh: 子溥靜，嗣。

translations.literal: His son Pujing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pujing succeeded.

sentences.zh: 二十六年八月，薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-sixth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twenty-sixth year he died.

sentences.zh: 九月，坐縱芘拳匪啟子毓麒，襲。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, for indulging and shielding Boxer bandits and provoking hostilities, his title was taken; as he had already died he was spared further punishment; his younger brother's son Yugi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was posthumously stripped of his title for indulging and shielding the Boxer bandits and provoking hostilities. Because he had already died he was spared further punishment, and his younger brother's son Yugi succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 寧良郡王弘晈，允祥第四子。

translations.literal: Prince Ningliang of the Second Rank Hongjiao was Yinxiang's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ningliang of the Second Rank Hongjiao was the fourth son of Yinxiang.

sentences.zh: 世宗褒允祥功，加封郡王，任王於諸子中指封，允祥固辭不敢承。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor praised Yinxiang's merit, additionally enfeoffing him as prince of the second rank and permitting the prince to designate one of his sons for enfeoffment by pointing; Yinxiang steadfastly declined and did not dare accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor praised Yinxiang's service, promoted him again to prince of the second rank, and allowed him to designate one of his sons for enfeoffment by pointing among them. Yinxiang steadfastly declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 及允祥薨，世宗乃封弘？

translations.literal: When Yinxiang died, the Shizong Emperor then enfeoffed Hongjiao
translations.idiomatic: When Yinxiang died, the Yongzheng Emperor enfeoffed Hongjiao

sentences.zh: 寧郡王，世襲。

translations.literal: as Prince Ning of the second rank, with hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: as Prince Ning of the second rank, with hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十九年八月，薨，諡曰良。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-ninth year of Qianlong he died; his posthumous title was Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twenty-ninth year of the Qianlong reign he died and was posthumously styled Liang.

sentences.zh: 子永福，仍循例襲貝勒。

translations.literal: His son Yongfu still succeeded according to precedent as beile.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongfu succeeded as beile according to the usual rule.

sentences.zh: 四十七年九月，薨，諡恭恪。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the forty-seventh year he died; his posthumous title was Gongke.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the forty-seventh year he died and was posthumously styled Gongke.

sentences.zh: 子綿譽，仍襲貝勒。

translations.literal: His son Mianyu still succeeded as beile.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mianyu likewise succeeded as beile.

sentences.zh: 子孫遞降，以鎮國公世襲。

translations.literal: Descendants declined in rank by degrees, with zhenguo gong succeeding hereditarily.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants declined in rank by successive generations, the title passing hereditarily as zhenguo gong.

sentences.zh: 載敦紹封怡親王，即以載泰襲鎮國公。

translations.literal: Zaidun was enfeoffed in succession as Prince Yi, and Zaitai succeeded as zhenguo gong.
translations.idiomatic: Zaidun was enfeoffed in succession as Prince Yi, while Zaitai succeeded as zhenguo gong.

sentences.zh: 允祥諸子：弘昌，初封貝子，進貝勒，坐事奪爵；

translations.literal: Yinxiang's sons: Hongchang, first enfeoffed as beizi, promoted to beile, then stripped of his title for an offense;
translations.idiomatic: Yinxiang's sons: Hongchang was first enfeoffed as beizi, promoted to beile, and later stripped of his title for an offense;

sentences.zh: 弘暾，未封早世，聘於富察氏，未婚守志，世宗愍之，命視貝勒例殯葬；

translations.literal: Hongdun died young without enfeoffment; betrothed to a lady of the Fuca clan, she remained faithful though unmarried; the Shizong Emperor commiserated and ordered burial according to the beile precedent;
translations.idiomatic: Hongdun died young without receiving a title; betrothed to a lady of the Fuca clan, she remained faithful though unmarried. The Yongzheng Emperor commiserated and ordered that he be buried according to the beile precedent;

sentences.zh: 弘昑，亦用其例。

translations.literal: Hongqin was also treated by that precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Hongqin was likewise buried according to that precedent.

sentences.zh: 恂勤郡王允禵，聖祖第十四子。

translations.literal: Prince Xunqin of the Second Rank Yinti was Kangxi's fourteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xunqin of the Second Rank Yinti was Kangxi's fourteenth son.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十八年，封貝子。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year of Kangxi he was enfeoffed as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year of the Kangxi reign he was enfeoffed as beizi.

sentences.zh: 五十年，從上幸塞外。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year he accompanied the emperor on a journey beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year he accompanied the emperor on a journey beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 自是輒從。

translations.literal: From then on he always accompanied.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he always accompanied the emperor on such journeys.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，賜銀四千兩。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year four thousand taels of silver were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year he was granted four thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，命為撫遠大將軍，討策妄阿喇布坦。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he was appointed Grand General for the Pacification of the Distance to campaign against Tsewang Araptan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year he was appointed Grand General for the Pacification of the Distance to campaign against Tsewang Araptan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，師行，上御太和殿授印，命用正黃旗纛。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the army set out; the emperor presided at the Hall of Supreme Harmony to confer the seal and ordered the use of the Plain Yellow Banner standard.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the army set out. The emperor presided at the Hall of Supreme Harmony to confer the seal and ordered that the Plain Yellow Banner standard be used.

sentences.zh: 五十八年四月，劾吏部侍郎色爾圖督兵餉失職，都統胡錫圖索詐騷擾，治其罪。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifty-eighth year he impeached Vice Minister of Personnel Sertu for dereliction in supervising troops and supplies, and Commander Hu Xitu for extortion and harassment; their crimes were punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifty-eighth year he impeached Vice Minister of Personnel Sertu for dereliction in supervising troops and supplies and Commander Hu Xitu for extortion and harassment; both were punished.

sentences.zh: 都統延信疏稱：「準噶爾與青海聯姻婭，大將軍領兵出口，必有諜告準酋者，不若暫緩前進。

translations.literal: Commander Yanxin memorialized: "The Dzungars are allied by marriage with Qinghai; when the grand general leads troops beyond the frontier there will certainly be spies informing the Dzungar chief—better to pause the advance for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Yanxin memorialized: "The Dzungars are allied by marriage with Qinghai. When the grand general leads troops beyond the frontier, spies will certainly inform the Dzungar chief. It would be better to pause the advance for the moment.

sentences.zh: 」上命駐西寧。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered encampment at Xining.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered the army to encamp at Xining.

sentences.zh: 五十九年正月，允禵移軍穆魯斯烏蘇，遣平逆將軍延信率師入西藏，令宗查布防西寧，訥爾素防古木。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifty-ninth year Yinti moved his army to Murusi Usu, dispatched General for the Pacification of Rebellion Yanxin to lead troops into Tibet, ordered Zongcha to defend Xining, and Ne'ersu to defend Gumu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifty-ninth year Yinti moved his army to Murusi Usu, dispatched General for the Pacification of Rebellion Yanxin to lead troops into Tibet, ordered Zongcha to defend Xining, and Ne'ersu to defend Gumu.

sentences.zh: 時別立新胡必爾汗，遣兵送之入藏。

translations.literal: At that time a new Qoshot Khan was installed and troops were sent to escort him into Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a new Qoshot Khan was installed and troops were dispatched to escort him into Tibet.

sentences.zh: 十月，延信擊敗準噶爾將策零敦多卜等於卜克河諸地。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Yanxin defeated the Dzungar generals Tsewang Donjub and others at various places along the Boke River.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Yanxin defeated the Dzungar generals Tsewang Donjub and others at various places along the Boke River.

sentences.zh: 六十年五月，允禵率師駐甘州，進萬？

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixtieth year Yinti led his army to encamp at Ganzhou and advanced
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixtieth year Yinti led his army to encamp at Ganzhou and advanced

sentences.zh: 次吐魯番。

translations.literal: then halted at Turfan.
translations.idiomatic: and then halted at Turfan.

sentences.zh: 旋請於明年進兵。

translations.literal: Soon he requested to advance the army the following year.
translations.idiomatic: He soon requested permission to advance the army the following year.

sentences.zh: 閏六月，和爾博斯厄穆齊寨桑以厄魯特兵五百圍回民，回餘人乞援。

translations.literal: In the intercalary sixth month the zaisang of Korbos Emuqi encircled Hui people with five hundred Oirat troops; the surviving Hui people pleaded for aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary sixth month the zaisang of Korbos Emuqi besieged Hui communities with five hundred Oirat troops, and the survivors pleaded for relief.

sentences.zh: 允禵以糧運艱阻，兵難久駐，若徙入內地，亦苦糧少地狹，哈密扎薩克額敏皆不能容，布隆吉爾、達里圖諸地又阻瀚海，請諭靖逆將軍富寧安相機援撫，從之。

translations.literal: Yinti, because grain transport was difficult and troops could not remain long, and because if they moved into the interior they would also suffer from scarce grain and narrow land—Hami's jasaq Emin could not accommodate them all, and Bulungir, Dalitu, and other places were blocked by the desert sea—requested that Grand General for the Pacification of Rebellion Funing'an be instructed to give aid and reassurance as circumstances allowed; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Yinti reported that grain transport was arduous and the army could not remain long on campaign. If the troops were moved into the interior they would still suffer from scarce provisions and cramped terrain; Hami's jasaq Emin could not accommodate them, and Bulungir, Dalitu, and other places were cut off by the desert. He asked that Grand General for the Pacification of Rebellion Funing'an be instructed to give aid and reassurance as circumstances allowed, and his request was approved.

sentences.zh: 十月，召來京，面授方略。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was summoned to the capital and personally received strategy.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was summoned to the capital, where the emperor personally instructed him in strategy.

sentences.zh: 六十一年三月，還軍。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixty-first year he returned to the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixty-first year he returned to the army.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，諭總理王大臣曰：「西路軍務，大將軍職任重大，但於皇考大事若不來京，恐於心不安，速行文大將軍王馳驛來京。

translations.idiomatic: He made spirit vessels in the form of tripods, ritual bronzes, plates, and bowls and placed them beside his couch and table.

sentences.zh: 三十年，薨，予諡。

translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he died and was granted a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 子永璧，襲。

translations.idiomatic: His son Yongbi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，薨，諡曰勤。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he died; his posthumous title was Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he died; his posthumous title was Qin.

translations.idiomatic: His son Mianlun inherited as Prince of the Second Rank.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，薨，諡曰謹。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he died; his posthumous title was Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year he died; his posthumous title was Jin.

sentences.zh: 弟綿循，襲。

translations.literal: His younger brother Mianxun inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Mianxun inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十二年，薨，諡曰恪。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Jiaqing he died; his posthumous title was Ke.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of the Jiaqing reign he died; his posthumous title was Ke.

sentences.zh: 子奕亨，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: His son Yiheng inherited as beile.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yiheng inherited as beile.

sentences.zh: 卒，子載容，襲貝子。

translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Zairong inherited as beizi.

sentences.zh: 同治中，加貝勒銜。

translations.literal: During the Tongzhi reign he was granted the rank of beile.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongzhi reign he was granted the rank of beile.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡敏恪。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Minke.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his posthumous title was Minke.

sentences.zh: 子溥廉，襲鎮國公。

translations.literal: His son Pulian inherited as Duke of the State Supporting the Nation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pulian inherited as Duke of the State Supporting the Nation.

sentences.zh: 懷親王福惠，世宗第七子。

translations.literal: Prince Huai Fuhui was the Shizong Emperor's seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai Fuhui was the Yongzheng Emperor's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 八歲殤。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eight.
